entries.question: How do I format a note?

content.text: Tap the note in a visit, time entry, plan, or trip to open the note editor. The bar above the keyboard adds headings, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, bulleted and numbered lists, checklists, and links. Swipe the bar sideways to see every button; the button at its right end puts the keyboard away. Your note is kept with the visit, entry, plan, or trip when you tap Save or Add. Links show a preview card under the note, and you can tick off checklist items right where the note is shown. Service report comments and follow-up topics stay plain text.

entries.question: How do I add photos to a note?

content.text: In the note editor, tap the photo button, then Take Photo or Choose Photos. A note holds up to 10 photos. To make one smaller or bigger, tap it while editing and drag a corner; it keeps that share of the note's width on every device. Photos are resized and saved on this device; tap one in a note to see it full screen or share it. With data protection mode on, visit notes can't hold photos, because a photo of someone's home is personal information about them. Photos reach your other devices only when Include photos is on in iCloud Sync (Google Drive Sync on Android); Cloud Sync doesn't carry photos yet. Backup files and contact shares leave them out. A Plan you invite buddies to shares its note's photos too, end-to-end encrypted; a buddy sees a placeholder until a photo finishes downloading, or while photo sharing is paused. Shared photos are deleted from WitnessWork's servers a month after the Plan, or right away when you remove them, delete the Plan, or stop sharing it.

entries.question: Why is a photo missing from a note, or a note plain on another device?

content.text: A note says “This photo isn't on this device” when the photo hasn't reached this device: photo sync is off here or on the device that added it, or the photo is still uploading. Turn on Include photos in iCloud Sync (Google Drive Sync on Android) on both devices and open the app on the device that added the photo; the photo appears after the next sync. Cloud Sync doesn't carry photos yet, so on Cloud Sync a photo stays on the device that added it. Restoring a backup file doesn't bring photos back. A device with an older version of WitnessWork shows notes as plain text, without formatting or photos, and editing a note there replaces its formatting everywhere. Update WitnessWork on every device to keep it.

entries.question: How do I resize or hide the sidebar on my tablet?

content.text: On a wide tablet window on iOS or Android, drag the small bar halfway down the sidebar's right edge to resize it. Narrowing the sidebar hides destination names and leaves their icons; widen it to show the names again. Tap Hide sidebar beside WitnessWork (at the top of the icon-only sidebar) to hide navigation completely. Tap Show sidebar in the page header to restore your last saved width. Your width and visibility are saved on this device across app restarts; they are not synced or included in ministry backups, and resizing does not change your records. The sidebar needs a window at least 1,000 points wide and a supported text size. In a narrower window or with very large text, the bottom bar returns automatically; widen the window or rotate to landscape to use the sidebar again. Screen reader users can adjust the Resize sidebar control to increase or decrease its width. If the navigation still seems missing, restart the app and use Still need help? below; keep contact details and other private data out of public reports.

entries.question: How do I use the menu bar on iPad?

content.text: On iPadOS 26 or later, use Windowed Apps or Stage Manager and swipe down from the top edge to reveal the menu bar. After setup, WitnessWork Preferences opens in-app settings; the standard Settings item opens your device's settings. File opens Log Visit…, Add Time when hours logging is enabled, Add Contact, New Plan, and Backup & Restore. Edit → Find Contact opens the Contacts list and focuses search. Help opens the Help Center, What's New, your email app for private support, or Check for Update. These shortcuts reuse the existing screens; opening a form does not save or share your records. Check for Update checks for a compatible app update and uses the existing download and restart flow when one is available. It cannot install a new native app version, and is unavailable in development builds. Menu-bar support requires an installed app build that includes it and is unavailable on iPhone and Android. If items are missing, update from your app store and reopen WitnessWork. You can still use the same actions inside the app. For other problems, use the Help Center's private email link and keep contact details and backups out of public reports.

entries.question: How do I lock WitnessWork with Face ID or Touch ID?

content.text: Open Settings → Security and turn on Require Face ID (Require Touch ID or Require Passcode on devices without Face ID; Require Biometric Unlock on Android). WitnessWork asks you to confirm it's you before it turns on. From then on, WitnessWork asks you to unlock it every time it opens. Use Require to choose whether it asks again as soon as you leave the app, or only after 1, 5, or 15 minutes away. If Face ID, Touch ID, or your fingerprint isn't recognized, use your device passcode, PIN, pattern, or password instead. The lock is on this device only: it isn't synced, saved in backups, or sent anywhere, so turn it on separately on each device. Your device needs a passcode, or on Android a screen lock (PIN, pattern, or password); if your Android device has none, tap Open Settings when WitnessWork asks, set one up, then turn the lock on again. If you remove it later, WitnessWork opens without asking. While the lock is on, the app switcher (Recents on Android) shows a blank card instead of WitnessWork's screen; on Android, this needs Android 13 or later. The lock covers the app itself; widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri, and your watch still show what they normally do. Messages, celebrations, and Update Required wait until you unlock, and a reminder, widget, or link you tap while WitnessWork is locked opens once you unlock. To turn it off, open Settings → Security, turn the switch off, and confirm it's you. If unlocking keeps failing, check that your device passcode works on the lock screen, then force-quit and reopen WitnessWork. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep personal details out of public reports.

entries.question: Why does WitnessWork say Update Required?

content.text: Sometimes WitnessWork's server changes in a way older versions of the app can't follow. When your version is too old to work with it, WitnessWork shows Update Required with your version and the one you need, and waits until you update. Tap Update WitnessWork to open the App Store, or the Google Play Store app on Android, install the update, then open WitnessWork again. If App Lock is on, unlock WitnessWork first; Update Required appears right after. While it shows, WitnessWork stops contacting its server, so Cloud Sync, Backup, Buddies, and Scribe AI wait. Your service records, contacts, and notes stay on your device and are all there after the update; changes that hadn't synced yet sync then, and Backup runs again a few seconds after you open the updated app. If the store doesn't open, open it yourself and search for WitnessWork. If it doesn't show an update, close the store app, open it again, and check for updates there.

entries.question: How do I navigate with keyboard shortcuts on iPad?

content.text: Connect a hardware keyboard to an iPad running iPadOS 26 or later, then hold Command while the main navigation is visible. Small shortcut labels appear beside the bottom tabs or sidebar items. Press Command and the displayed number to open that screen; release Command to hide the labels. Numbers follow the visible navigation order, so by default Home is Command 1 and Contacts is Command 2. Other numbers depend on which items are visible, including Settings in the sidebar. Close any open form or other screen before using these navigation shortcuts; they do not save or discard records. Only shortcut use is measured, not what you type. Support requires an installed app build with the keyboard feature and is unavailable on iPhone and Android. If labels do not appear, check that the keyboard is connected, return to the main navigation, and update and reopen the app. You can always tap navigation items instead. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep contact details out of public reports.

entries.question: How do I use a trackpad, mouse, or Apple Pencil on iPad?

content.text: Connect a trackpad or mouse to your iPad, or hover a supported Apple Pencil just above the screen. Buttons, rows, and calendar days highlight as the pointer moves over them. When the sidebar is narrowed to icons, resting the pointer on an icon shows its name; other icon-only buttons, such as the map controls and Notifications, also show their names. Hover over the activity grid, the Service Year pace chart, or a mileage bar to see its date and value. On the map, hover a pin to see the contact's name, or hover a contact in the map's side list to name its pin. A secondary click (two-finger click) opens the same menu and preview as touching and holding. The sidebar's resize bar shows arrows for the directions it can still move, and two-finger scrolling moves a contact photo while you crop it. Everything is still available by touch: tap, touch and hold, or drag as usual. Hover changes nothing in your records. Only the fact that a pointer or Pencil was used is measured, at most once a day; no positions, names, or values are sent. On Android, a mouse highlights rows and shows names and chart values, but pins on the map don't show names on hover. iPhone has no hover. If nothing responds, check that the trackpad, mouse, or Pencil is connected, then update and reopen the app. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep contact details out of public reports.

entries.question: How do I log time or plan a specific day?

content.text: Tap the day on the Schedule tab, in This Week on Home, or under All Days on the Progress tab. The day opens in the bottom half of the screen, so the calendar or list you tapped stays in view above it, and you can tap another day there to switch to it. If the day has no time logged yet, tap Add Time under Time Reports to unfold the time form right there: tap Time, choose how long, add a note or Type if you like, and tap Submit. If the day has no plans yet, tap Plan Day under Plans the same way: add a title if you like, choose One Time or Recurring and how long, and tap the Add button. Tap Add Time or Plan Day again to fold the form away. To add more time or another plan, tap + beside Time Reports or Plans. Tap an entry to change or delete it, or tap a plan to open it. To log a plan you kept, touch and hold it and choose Log as Time; its length and Type are filled in. These open the form in the same place, and its back arrow returns to the day without saving. A note opens in the note editor over the whole screen; tap Done and the day comes back with the form as you left it. To see more of the day or more of the screen above it, drag the bar at the top of the day up or down; WitnessWork remembers the size on this device. To close the day, tap the X or drag it all the way down; on Android, the back button works too. Logging time appears only if your status logs hours; Kingdom Publishers turn on Log my hours in Settings → Profile first.

entries.question: Does my time automatically roll over to the next month?

content.text: Yes. Partial hours below your monthly goal can carry over to the next month. Open Settings → Profile → Advanced and turn on Automatic time rollover (shown when you log hours). The carried hours appear automatically when the new month begins, so you don't need to manually subtract or re-enter anything.

entries.question: How are Bible studies counted?

content.text: Studies are tracked per contact, not per day. To count a study, open a contact, log a conversation, and mark it as "Conducted Bible Study." That contact will count as 1 study for the current month, even if you have multiple sessions with them. To raise your study count, mark a study conversation with a different contact. Visits that came with a contact someone shared with you are theirs, so they don't count; once you log your own study with that contact, it counts.

entries.question: Can I sync my data between devices?

content.text: iCloud Sync is a Supporter feature on iOS. Open Settings → Device Sync on each supported device, choose iCloud, and use the same iCloud account to sync your service records, contacts, visits, and preferences. Photos have a separate Include images in sync switch. Without an internet connection, the status says Waiting for connection; your changes are saved on the device and sync when you're back online. If a device signs in to a different Apple Account, iCloud Sync turns off there before any records are read or sent, and they stay on the device; turn sync back on to choose how to combine it with that account’s iCloud data. That device also stops sharing Supporter status from your previous account; if it was bought with this device’s App Store account, use Restore Purchases. A device set up from another device’s backup syncs as its own device automatically. Calendar Sync is a separate, free feature that publishes your upcoming Follow-ups to a dedicated calendar; it does not sync your app records between devices. Cloud Sync, the other option in Settings → Device Sync, is end-to-end encrypted and also syncs between an iPhone and an Android phone (see “What is Cloud Sync?”). A device syncs with one option at a time, and only with your devices on the same option, so choose the same one on each. On Android, Supporters can also sync between Android phones and tablets with Google Drive Sync (see “How do I sync my data between Android devices?”). To move to a new phone, including from an iPhone to an Android phone, see “How do I move to a new phone or switch between iPhone and Android?”.

entries.question: How do I sync my data between Android devices?

content.text: Google Drive Sync is a Supporter feature on Android, in beta. On each Android phone or tablet, open Settings → Device Sync, choose Google Drive, and turn on Sync with Google Drive, then choose the same Google Account in Google's window and allow WitnessWork to keep its data in your Google Drive. It syncs your service records, plans, contacts, visits, categories, mileage, profile, and shared preferences; photos have a separate Include images in sync switch. Each device has its own switch, and settings like data protection mode, analytics consent, and onboarding stay on each device. While WitnessWork is open, changes from your other devices arrive within about a minute, and otherwise the next time you open it; tap Sync now to check right away. On a new Android device, choose From Google Drive on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen to restore your data, which also brings your Supporter status over once that Google Account is connected. If a device connects a different Google Account, sync turns off there before anything is read or sent, and your records stay on the device. Google Drive Sync syncs only with your other Android devices that use it. To sync between an iPhone and an Android device, use Cloud Sync in Settings → Device Sync instead (see “What is Cloud Sync?”). To move your records to another phone, use Cloud Sync, Backup in Settings → Account, or a backup file from Settings → Backup & Restore.

entries.question: What does Google Drive Sync store, and who can see it?

content.text: Each Android device keeps one copy of your WitnessWork data, plus optional photos, in a hidden app folder in the Google Drive of the account you connected. Only WitnessWork can open that folder: it doesn't appear in the Drive app or website, other apps can't read it, and WitnessWork can't see anything else in your Drive. Your data goes straight between your device and Google and never passes through WitnessWork's servers. Google stores it under your Google Account like your other Drive files; it isn't end-to-end encrypted. WitnessWork keeps only a one-way code for the connected account on the device, not your email. The folder counts against your Google storage. To remove it, turn off sync on every device, then in Google Drive on the web open Settings → Manage apps → WitnessWork → Options → Delete hidden app data. Disconnecting Google Drive in Settings → Device Sync stops access from that device and leaves the folder for your other devices. To remove WitnessWork's access for every device, remove it under Third-party apps & services in your Google Account. Your JSON backups from Settings → Backup & Restore are separate and stay wherever you save them.

entries.question: Google Drive Sync isn't working on my Android device. What can I check?

content.text: Open Settings → Device Sync and read the status. Check that every device uses Google Drive and is connected to the same Google Account and that Google Play services is installed and up to date. If the status says to reconnect, tap Reconnect Google Drive and allow access again; Google asks again if access was removed in your Google Account settings. If your Google storage is full, your changes stay on this device until there's room; free up space or get more storage, then tap Sync now. Sync needs an internet connection; the status says Waiting for connection until you're back online, and changes made offline are sent then while WitnessWork is open. If it says Google Drive is busy, Google is limiting requests for a while; your changes stay on this device and sync tries again on its own. If a device uses a newer version of WitnessWork, update every device. Google Drive Sync requires Supporter access; if it lapses, sync pauses and resumes when access returns. Keep an exported backup and the device with your latest data before rebuilding Google Drive data. Contact private support from the Help Center if syncing still fails, and keep householder details out of public reports.

entries.question: How do I show Follow-ups in my calendar?

content.text: Calendar Sync is free on iPhone, iPad, and Android. This answer covers iPhone and iPad, and How does Calendar Sync work on Android? covers Android. During first-time setup, or from the invitation in the notifications tray after updating, tap Add to Calendar to create a WitnessWork calendar (in iCloud when available). You can also set it up anytime in Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync: allow full calendar access, then create a WitnessWork calendar or choose a calendar used only for WitnessWork. Updates need iCloud sign-in and an internet connection, even for Google or Outlook calendars. To use Google or Outlook, create a calendar with that provider, add the account in iPhone Settings → Apps → Calendar → Calendar Accounts, and turn on its calendars. Your default calendar and calendars stored only on this device can't be selected. Once a calendar is selected, every upcoming Follow-up is added automatically, including ones you already saved, as a 30-minute event. Calendar Sync adds all of your upcoming Follow-ups or none; to stop adding them, turn it off in Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync. Past Follow-ups, service Plans, and recurring Plans aren't added. Each event gets the same alert as its Follow-up's Notify Me reminder, and no alert when Notify Me is off. Your calendar provider may add its own default alerts; for Google, remove them under that calendar's Event notifications in Google Calendar settings. Make changes in WitnessWork, because calendar edits, including alerts, may be replaced on the next update.

entries.question: What does Calendar Sync share or store?

content.text: By default, published events contain a generic Follow-up title, the appointment time and duration, and a link that opens the Visit in WitnessWork. Include names and addresses is optional and applies across your devices; turning it on adds those details to published events. Visit notes and Follow-up topics are never exported. Your chosen calendar provider may sync events to other devices, shared calendars, and widgets, so check that calendar's sharing settings before including details. WitnessWork manages only events it marked as its own and does not import your personal calendar appointments. A private iCloud record stores device names and opaque identifiers, publishing ownership, the connected calendar's name and account label, shared options, and event identifiers. Appointment content stays in the chosen calendar account. Each device's calendar identifier and connection state stay local and are separate from app-data sync and backup files.

entries.question: Why does Calendar Sync use a primary device?

content.text: Exactly one device publishes your Follow-ups to avoid competing updates. The first device to connect becomes primary. On iOS devices using the same iCloud account, open Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync to register each device, view the Primary device list, and choose a primary. Calendar Sync itself does not require Supporter. Follow-ups edited on another device reach the primary through existing app-data sync, which still requires Supporter and sync turned on in Settings → Device Sync; open WitnessWork on the primary to publish them. After a transfer, the new primary needs access to the same calendar account and full calendar permission. If a transfer is pending, reopen WitnessWork on the previous primary so it can finish its interrupted operation. There is no automatic timeout takeover if that device is permanently unavailable; use private support under Still need help? in the Help Center. Removing a stale device from the list does not delete its app records or calendar events.

entries.question: Calendar events are missing or updates are paused. What should I do?

content.text: If Calendar Sync stops updating, a Calendar updates paused notification appears in the notifications tray (the bell on Home): right away when something needs you, such as calendar access, or after a day for problems that often clear on their own, like no internet connection. Tap it for the fix, or choose Turn Off if you no longer want Follow-ups in your calendar. You can also open Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync and read the displayed error. If WitnessWork needs calendar access, tap Open iPhone Settings, tap Calendars, and choose Full Access; Add Events Only isn't enough. When you come back to WitnessWork, setup or updates continue on their own. For connection problems, check your internet connection, iCloud sign-in, and calendar account, then tap Try Again. If setup says no calendar account can hold a WitnessWork calendar, turn on iCloud Calendars in iPhone Settings, then tap Try Again. Use Sync now on the primary device after your calendar account and app data finish syncing. A missing calendar must be reconnected or replaced; calendars renamed outside WitnessWork may need to be chosen again. When a previously published future event is missing, updates pause even if this device published it: calendar sync delays, deletion, and moving an event can look the same. Wait for the calendar account to finish syncing and confirm you chose the same dedicated calendar. Move any WitnessWork events you moved elsewhere back before retrying. Restore missing events is an explicit recovery option after those checks; it can create duplicates if copies are still downloading or remain elsewhere. A past Follow-up is not initially added. For pending device transfers, reopen the previous primary. If the problem continues, use the Help Center's private support option and include the app version, device and operating-system version, and the error shown. Keep contact details, calendar screenshots, notes, and backups out of public reports.

entries.question: What happens when I turn off Calendar Sync or uninstall WitnessWork?

content.text: In Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync, choose Turn Off Calendar Sync, or choose Turn Off on a Calendar updates paused notification. On the primary device, the one that updates your calendar, you can keep the events already added or remove them. Remove Events removes the marked events from the selected calendar, including previously exported history; unrelated events and the calendar itself remain. Turning it off on the primary stops updates from every device. On any other device, Calendar Sync turns off on that device only and the events stay. Events you keep, or that are left after uninstalling, are no longer updated until you set Calendar Sync up again. Uninstalling WitnessWork does not remove calendar events. You can remove an unused dedicated calendar in your calendar app after checking that it contains nothing you want to keep. Turning off Calendar Sync does not delete your Contacts, Visits, or Follow-ups in WitnessWork.

entries.question: How does Calendar Sync work on Android?

content.text: Calendar Sync is free on Android. During first-time setup, from the invitation in the notifications tray, or in Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync, tap Add to Calendar or Choose a calendar, then allow calendar access. Create a WitnessWork calendar on this device, or choose an existing calendar used only for WitnessWork, such as one you created in Google Calendar and set to sync to this phone. A calendar created on the device stays on this device; a Google calendar also shows on your other devices and on the web. Main calendars can't be selected. Every upcoming Follow-up is then added as a 30-minute event with the same alert as its Notify Me reminder; Calendar Sync adds all of your upcoming Follow-ups or none. Past Follow-ups and Plans aren't added. Updates run when you open WitnessWork and after you save changes, and Sync now updates right away. Each event's description holds a WitnessWork link that identifies its Follow-up, so an update changes the existing event instead of adding another, even when another Android device updates the same Google calendar. Don't edit that link. An event you delete in your calendar app comes back on the next update. Android has no primary device and doesn't use iCloud, and Include names and addresses applies to this device only. If updates stop, for example because calendar access was turned off, a Calendar updates paused notification appears in the notifications tray; tap it for the fix, or open Calendar Sync to read the error. For calendar access, tap Open Settings, then Permissions → Calendar → Allow; setup or updates continue when you come back to WitnessWork. For other errors, tap Try Again. Turn Off Calendar Sync keeps or removes WitnessWork events; it never deletes the calendar or your other events. Uninstalling WitnessWork leaves its events, so remove them first if you don't want them. If the problem continues, use the private support option under Still need help? in the Help Center, and keep contact details and calendar screenshots out of public reports.

entries.question: Are there home or lock screen widgets?

content.text: Yes, on iOS. Long-press your home or lock screen, tap the + button, search for WitnessWork, and pick the widget you want. Service Report shows this month's hours toward your goal and how much a day it takes to reach it, on your home or lock screen; if you don't log hours, it shows this month's conversations and studies, counted as in the app. Calendar, Appointments, Contacts, and Pet Companion go on your home screen. Widgets move on to the new day at midnight even if you don't open WitnessWork; if one looks out of date, open the app.

entries.question: Is there an Apple Watch app?

content.text: Yes, for iPhone with an Apple Watch on watchOS 26 or later. It installs automatically if Automatic App Install is on; otherwise open the Watch app on your iPhone, find WitnessWork under Available Apps, and tap Install. Then open WitnessWork on your iPhone once so your watch gets your progress. The watch shows this month's hours and whether you're ahead of or behind your plans, counted the same way as on your iPhone (without plans, how much a day it takes to reach your goal). On the watch you can add time for today with an optional Type, start and pause your iPhone's timer, and save the timer's time as an entry. If you don't log hours as a Kingdom Publisher, you can mark that you shared the good news this month. Two complications can go on a watch face or in your Smart Stack: Monthly Progress shows your hours toward this month's goal, with a mark where your plans put you by today; in a round spot you can choose a ring or a gauge, with your goal at its end or a clock below, and without a goal it shows your hours alone. Up Next shows your next follow-up or plan. You can also use Siri on your watch to add time, start, pause or stop your timer, and log a mileage trip, with the same phrases as on iPhone, such as "Add time in WitnessWork" or "Log a trip in WitnessWork". Your iPhone keeps your records. The watch receives your monthly progress, report status, timer, Types, car names and distance unit, and for Up Next the name, address and topic of your follow-ups and the title and place of your plans for the next two weeks. It never receives notes or other contact details, and it can't edit or delete entries. The watch app needs your iPhone, so it isn't available for an Apple Watch set up with Family Setup. With an Android phone, use the Wear OS app instead.

entries.question: Why does my Apple Watch say Syncing with iPhone?

content.text: Time and trips you add on your watch are sent to your iPhone right away when it's nearby, or the next time they connect, and saved once WitnessWork runs on your iPhone. Until then your watch shows Syncing with iPhone. Its total and complications include that time right away, except Credit Time, which is added once your iPhone saves it and applies your monthly credit limit. Each entry keeps the day you added it on the watch, is saved only once even if it's sent again, and isn't brought back if you already deleted it on your iPhone. Saved entries reach your other devices with sync like any other entry. Starting, pausing, stopping and saving the timer need your iPhone nearby. If the watch says the timer changed on your iPhone, check the time and try again. If your iPhone can't save an entry, the watch tells you instead of confirming it, and the time isn't added; if it asks you to update WitnessWork on your iPhone, update it and try again. If your watch stays out of date, or its complications show — after a week without an update, keep your iPhone nearby and unlocked, open WitnessWork on your iPhone, then open it on your watch. After your iPhone restarts, unlock it once before syncing. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your records out of public reports.

entries.question: What does Up Next on my Apple Watch show?

content.text: Up Next shows whichever comes first: your next follow-up or your next plan. Plans appear only if you log hours. Add the Up Next complication to a watch face or your Smart Stack: touch and hold your watch face and tap Edit, or use the Watch app on your iPhone. It's also on the watch app's home screen. A follow-up or plan stays up for 15 minutes after it starts, so you can check the address or topic when you arrive, and then the next one takes its place. A plan without a start time shows for its whole day, after that day's timed items. Missed follow-ups don't appear; find them in WitnessWork on your iPhone. Names and topics are hidden while your wrist is down or your watch is locked, because others may see your watch face. Tap Up Next to open it, then tap Directions for directions in Maps on your watch, or Start Timer to start your iPhone's service timer for a plan; the timer needs your iPhone nearby. Up Next looks two weeks ahead and keeps moving along while your iPhone is away. Changes you make on your iPhone reach your watch the next time they connect. If it's out of date, open WitnessWork on your iPhone, then on your watch. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep householder details out of public reports.

entries.question: Is there a Wear OS app?

content.text: Yes, for an Android phone with a watch on Wear OS 3 or later. Install WitnessWork from the Play Store on your watch, or from WitnessWork's Play Store page on your phone, then open WitnessWork on your phone once so your watch gets your progress. The watch shows this month's hours and whether you're ahead of or behind your plans, counted the same way as on your phone (without plans, how much a day it takes to reach your goal). On the watch you can add time for today with an optional Type, start and pause your phone's timer, and save the timer's time as an entry. If you don't log hours as a Kingdom Publisher, you can mark that you shared the good news this month. Add the Monthly Progress and Up Next complications to a watch face, and the Monthly Progress tile to start or pause your timer or add time with a swipe. While your timer runs, it shows on your watch face with Pause and Stop; Stop adds the timer's whole minutes as an entry for today. Allow notifications when your watch asks, so the running timer can show there. Your phone keeps your records. The watch receives your monthly progress, report status, timer, Types, car names and distance unit, and for Up Next the name, address and topic of your follow-ups and the title and place of your plans for the next two weeks. It never receives notes or other contact details, and it can't edit or delete entries. Because others may see your watch, Up Next shows "Follow Up" instead of a name on watch faces, and in the app while your wrist is down; open it to see who it is. Wear OS can't add time or log trips by voice, so use the tile or the app instead. The watch app needs your phone with WitnessWork installed.

entries.question: Why does my Wear OS watch say Syncing with phone?

content.text: Time you add on your watch is sent to your phone right away when it's nearby, or the next time they connect, and saved the next time you open WitnessWork on your phone. Until then your watch shows Syncing with phone. Its total, tile and complications include that time right away, except Credit Time, which is added once your phone saves it and applies your monthly credit limit. Each entry keeps the day you added it on the watch, is saved only once even if it's sent again, and isn't brought back if you already deleted it on your phone. Starting, pausing, stopping and saving the timer need your phone nearby, even if WitnessWork isn't open on it. If the watch says the timer changed on your phone, check the time and try again. If your phone can't save an entry, the watch tells you instead of confirming it, and the time isn't added; if it asks you to update WitnessWork on your phone, update it and try again. If your watch stays out of date, or its complications show — after a week without an update, check that it's connected to your phone in your watch's companion app, keep your phone nearby, open WitnessWork on your phone, then open it on your watch. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your records out of public reports.

entries.question: Can I use Siri or Shortcuts with WitnessWork?

content.text: Yes, on iPhone and iPad with iOS 17 or later, and on the Apple Watch app. Open WitnessWork once after updating, then say "Add time in WitnessWork", "Start my timer in WitnessWork", "Pause my timer in WitnessWork", "Stop my timer in WitnessWork", "Log a trip in WitnessWork" or "Log a round trip in WitnessWork". To add time you can also say log, enter, record, track or submit, and you can say how long, like "Log two hours in WitnessWork" or "Add 30 minutes to WitnessWork". Siri knows common amounts from 15 minutes to 12 hours; for any other amount, say "Add time in WitnessWork" and Siri asks how long. Siri listens in your Siri language, which can differ from the language you chose in WitnessWork. For trips, Siri asks how far. Distances use your Mileage distance unit; for a round trip, say the one-way distance and it's doubled. Stopping the timer adds its whole minutes as an entry for today and resets it; with less than a minute, nothing is added. Time and trips are added for today, as Standard time and with the car you used last. To pick a Type or car, add the action in the Shortcuts app, where you can also run it from the Action Button or a Home Screen shortcut. Adding time and the timer need you to log hours (Regular Publishers turn on Log my hours first). Logging trips needs Track Mileage on and at least one car. On iPhone and iPad the timer changes right away, and time and trips you add with Siri are saved the next time you open WitnessWork, then reach your other devices with sync like any entry. On the watch they're sent to your iPhone like other watch entries. Siri can only use your Types, car names, distance unit and timer from WitnessWork, never contacts, notes or reports. Siri and Shortcuts aren't available on Android. If Siri doesn't recognize a phrase, open WitnessWork once, wait a minute, and check that Siri is allowed for WitnessWork in Settings. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your records out of public reports.

entries.question: I'm a Kingdom Publisher. How do I log my hours?

content.text: Kingdom Publishers report only whether they shared in the ministry, so Home shows a Shared the Good News checkbox instead of Add Time. To keep track of your hours for yourself, open Settings → Profile and turn on Log my hours. Add Time, the timer, and the Progress tab appear, and you can set an optional Monthly Goal. WitnessWork asks about this once, during setup or in the notifications on Home. If you said no, you can turn it on in Settings anytime, and turning it off again hides those without deleting the time you logged. Your report still says only whether you shared, and any time you log also counts as sharing. If you're auxiliary pioneering this month, set that up instead in Settings → Profile: you'll log hours toward that month's goal, and the next month goes back to the checkbox.

entries.question: How do I switch between Publisher and Auxiliary Pioneer mid-month?

content.text: Open Settings → Profile → Status and choose what fits right now: Kingdom Publisher, Regular Auxiliary, Regular Pioneer, Special Pioneer, Circuit Overseer, or Custom. Goals and totals adjust to match. Switch back when you're done. Past months keep the time you entered, so your history stays accurate.

entries.question: Does the app submit my service report for me?

content.text: WitnessWork doesn't send your report anywhere by itself. How and to whom you submit is up to you and your service committee. Until last month's report is sent, the Service Report card on Home shows a Submit row for it, so you don't send this month's report before the month is over. If you already reported another way, touch and hold that row and choose Already Submitted. Open a month's Field Service Report, choose a method from the dropdown above the Submit button, and tap Submit. You can copy a plain-text summary, share it, or hand it straight to Hourglass or NW Publisher, which opens with your hours, Credit, and Bible studies filled in for you to review and send. NW Publisher only accepts the previous month's report. WitnessWork remembers your choice; you can also change it in Settings → Profile → Submission method. Once you submit, copy, or share a report, or tap Already Submitted on last month's reminder, the report and the month's card show Sent with the date. If that was a mistake, tap Sent at the top of the report, or press and hold the month's card, and choose Mark as Not Sent; last month's reminder then comes back. Opening Hourglass or NW Publisher counts only if it opens. If your device was offline when it opened, WitnessWork asks when you come back whether the report reached it, and marks it Sent only if you choose Mark as Sent. On Android, sharing doesn't mark the report, because the share sheet can't tell whether you sent it: after sending, tap Not Sent at the top of the report and choose Mark as Sent, or tap Already Submitted on the reminder.

entries.question: Can WitnessWork remind me when my report is ready to submit?

content.text: Yes. Go to Settings → Preferences → Plans and turn on Remind Me to Submit My Report, or tap Remind Me when the report screen offers it after you submit. On the 1st of each month you get a reminder at your Remind At time (9:00 AM unless you change it) that last month's report is ready. Tapping it opens that month's report, where you can review it and submit it with your usual method. WitnessWork never submits your report for you. There's no reminder for a month with nothing logged, or for a report you've already submitted from the report screen or marked as already submitted from the Home bell; submitting it after the reminder arrives clears it. Turning the setting on asks for notification permission, or opens your device settings if you've declined before. The reminder is worked out on your device from your own records and isn't sent anywhere. Each device schedules its own reminder, so open WitnessWork during the month to keep it current; if you submit on another device, open WitnessWork on this one so it knows. On Android, the system may deliver it a few minutes late to save battery. If it doesn't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings (on Android, including its Reminders category) and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. Last month's report is also listed in the Home bell until you submit it, even with notifications off. If it still doesn't work, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.

entries.question: What is WitnessWork Buddies, and why don't I see it?

content.text: Buddies lets you connect with up to five people you go out in service with and see each other's planned days, start times, and durations for the next eight weeks. You also see the badges each buddy shares. It works on iPhone, iPad, and Android, and buddies on different platforms can connect with each other. On the Schedule calendar, a buddy's photo or initial on a day means you're going out together, and a small dot under a day means other buddies plan to go out. Tap the day to see who. On iPhone and iPad, the Calendar widget shows the same marks and updates when WitnessWork refreshes Buddies, so open the app if it looks behind. It is free when available, and needs WitnessWork from the App Store or Google Play on a device that can be verified (see "Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?"). Open Schedule, tap Buddies at the top, and complete the introduction with your profile name. A dot on that button means a request is waiting for you to confirm. Buddies may be unavailable during rollout. Update the installed app if the Buddies button is missing. If the button is dimmed, Buddies is temporarily unavailable; your saved buddies stay on your calendar, so try again later.

entries.question: How do I add a buddy, and who confirms the request?

content.text: Open Buddies from Schedule, or tap Invite Buddies on a new Plan before you have a buddy, and tap Invite a Buddy or the + button to share a Buddies Invite. To pair in person, use the code button to show your Buddies Code and have the other person scan it inside WitnessWork. You can also paste a link through Enter Invite Link. The recipient taps Accept; the person who created the invite then opens Buddies → Requests and taps Confirm. You start seeing each other's plans only after that confirmation. Confirm only the person you intended to invite.

entries.question: Why is my Buddies Invite waiting, expired, or saying all spots are in use?

content.text: An accepted request waits until the inviter confirms it in Buddies → Requests. Each Buddies Invite works once and expires after seven days; ask for a new link if it was used, cancelled, or expired. Your five spots include buddies and pending invites or requests. Cancel an unused invite or remove a buddy to make room. If making an invite fails because the connection dropped, tap Try Again: if the first invite was made after all, WitnessWork shows that one instead of making another, and it's listed with your pending invites so you can share or cancel it. Only a limited number of unused invite links can be open at once. If tapping an invite link opens a web page instead of WitnessWork, install WitnessWork from the App Store or Google Play and tap the link again, or copy the link and paste it in Buddies → Enter Invite Link. If scanning is unavailable, allow camera access in your device's settings or share and paste the invite link instead.

entries.question: What can my buddies see, and is sharing private?

content.text: Buddies always see your name and the days you plan to go out over the next eight weeks, with how long you plan. Your photo (which buddies can tap to see full size), pioneer status, streak, badges, pet (its kind, coat, and name), and your Plans' start times are shared unless you turn them off in Buddies Settings. Badges go without progress, counts, or dates. Under Your Plans, Start times can share the exact time, only the time of day (Morning, Afternoon, or Evening), or no time at all, and Pause sharing hides your plans, streak, badges, and pet from every buddy for a week, a month, or until you turn it back on. Each of these can be different for one buddy: open their page and tap Sharing & Alerts. Buddies aren't told when you change any of this. Calendar sharing never includes your recorded service time, reports, goals, categories, contact list, visit history, or notes. Shared content is end-to-end encrypted so only you and the buddies you choose can read it. WitnessWork's server knows you only by an anonymous account number your device made, never your name, email, or phone number. Explicit Plan and Follow-up invitations share extra details, including a Plan's note (and its photos) or a Follow-up's address; check those details before inviting someone. Find the Privacy Policy under Still need help?, using the support button in this screen's header.

entries.question: Can I pause sharing or hide when I go out?

content.text: Yes. Open Buddies, tap the menu button, and choose Buddies Settings. Under Your Plans, Start times sets how precisely buddies see when you go out: Exact time, Time of day (Morning before noon, Afternoon until 5 PM, Evening after that), or Don't share. Buddies still see which days you plan and for how long. Pause sharing hides your plans, streak, badges, and pet from every buddy for a week, a month, or until you turn it back on; they still see your name and photo, and new badges aren't announced. While a pause is on, Buddies shows Sharing is paused with a Resume button. A timed pause ends by itself, and your plans return to buddies the next time WitnessWork refreshes Buddies on your device. To stop sharing plans with just one buddy, open their page, tap Sharing & Alerts, and turn off Share my plans; a pause still covers them too. Buddies aren't told about any of these choices, though they may notice your plans are gone. Plan and Follow-up invitations you send still go out while sharing is paused. Your choices apply on all your devices with Buddies. Your photo, pioneer status, streak, badges, and pet each have their own switch under How buddies see you.

entries.question: Can I share different things with different buddies?

content.text: Yes. Buddies Settings starts with All Buddies: the settings every buddy follows. To change any of them for one buddy, tap Choose a buddy at the top of Buddies Settings (All Buddies / Choose a buddy) and pick them, or open their page and tap Sharing & Alerts. You can choose, just for them, your photo, pioneer status, streak, badges, pet, whether they see your plans and how precisely start times show, whether their plans show on your calendar, and Ask to Join Alerts and Badge Alerts on this device. A setting that's theirs alone has a highlighted layers icon and an undo arrow beside its name: tap the undo arrow to have them follow All Buddies again, or the undo arrow at the top to do that for all of their settings. Tap the layers icon to see their value and All Buddies', with a checkmark on the one in use. In All Buddies, a setting some buddies have their own value for has a layers icon that lists them; tap a buddy there to open their settings. Tap All Buddies at the top to go back. Undo in the top corner takes back your changes on that screen, newest first. Changing an All Buddies setting changes it for every buddy who follows it, but not for a buddy with their own. Pause sharing is for everyone: while it's on, no buddy sees your plans, streak, badges, or pet, whatever their own settings. Your name always goes to every buddy, and buddies aren't told about any of these choices. Sharing and calendar settings apply on all your devices with Buddies; alerts apply only to the device you set them on.

entries.question: How do I invite a buddy to a Plan or Follow-up, and answer an invitation?

content.text: Use Invite Buddies when adding or editing a Plan or scheduled Follow-up, select confirmed buddies, and save. On a Plan's page, or a conversation's page for a scheduled Follow-up, Invite Buddies invites someone right away. You can also tap Invite to a Plan on a buddy's page. A Plan invite shares its date, time, duration, title, location, and note, with the note's formatting and photos. A Follow-up invite shares its date/time, the householder's first name, address or pin, and topic; those details expire a day after the visit. Check that you want to share these details with the people selected. Follow-up invitations are unavailable in Data Protection Mode. To reply, choose Going or Can't Make It in the notification bell on Home, on the buddy's page in Buddies, or on the invitation's own page (tap it in the bell, on the buddy's page, or on the day in Schedule to open it); you can change your answer later. A Follow-up invitation's page shows when your buddy is going, the householder's first name, the topic, and the place, with directions. An invitation stays in the bell until you answer it, it is canceled, or its Plan or Follow-up has happened, so it can't be dismissed or cleared by mistake; once answered, you can dismiss it. Going to a Plan adds a linked Plan to your schedule, which follows the inviter's changes or cancellation until the Plan happens; after that it stays on your schedule as it was. A buddy's shared Plan stays open to you for a month after it. Can't Make It takes it off your schedule, and switching back to Going on the Plan's page puts it back. If someone stops being your buddy before an invitation reaches them, WitnessWork tells you, and the Plan shows Not sent beside them until it has happened. A Follow-up invite does not import the contact or visit history.

entries.question: How do I ask to join a buddy's Plan?

content.text: Tap a day on your Schedule calendar, then tap Ask to Join next to a buddy who plans to go out that day. You can also tap one of their days under Next two weeks on their details screen. Your request shares only what you already see: the day, time, and length of their Plan. It shows as Asked until your buddy invites you, you withdraw it, or the Plan starts; tap Asked to withdraw it. Asking closes two hours before the Plan starts, and you can have up to three requests waiting with each buddy. Your buddy is alerted only the first time you ask for a Plan, and for at most three requests a day. If they move or remove that Plan, your request is withdrawn for you. Asked shows only on the device you asked from. When your buddy invites you, answer in the notification bell on Home. If you choose Going while you already have your own Plan at that time, one-time or recurring, you can replace it for that day so your time isn't counted twice. A recurring plan keeps going on your other days.

entries.question: How do I answer or turn off requests to join my Plans?

content.text: When a buddy asks to join one of your Plans, their request appears in the notification bell on Home. Tap Invite to add them to your Plan and send the invitation right away; the button turns into a check. Tap the request itself to open the Plan, where Invite works the same way. Tap Not Now (or dismiss it) to clear it quietly: your buddy is never told, and the request lapses when the Plan starts. If the Plan came from someone else's invitation, only its organizer can invite. Inviting someone to one date of a recurring plan turns that date into its own one-time Plan, and the recurring plan stays the same on your other days. If your Plans that day changed since they asked, open the Plan you're keeping to invite them. To stop alerts for every request, turn off Ask to Join Alerts in Buddies Settings. To stop alerts from one buddy, open their page, tap Sharing & Alerts, and turn off Ask to Join Alerts, or long-press their request and choose Turn Off Alerts. With alerts off for everyone, you can turn them on there for one buddy. Requests still appear in the bell either way. Not Now and these settings apply to this device only, so a request you cleared on one device can still show on another.

entries.question: What do Buddies notifications say, and who can see them?

content.text: Buddies notifications say who did what, using the nickname you gave that buddy if you set one: for example, “Anna invited you to a Plan” with its day and time, “Joe can't make it,” “Levi would like to join you,” or “Levi earned a badge” with the badge's name. A Follow-up notification shows only its day and time, never the householder's name, address, or topic, and a Plan notification never shows its title, place, or note. WitnessWork's server never sees these names or details: each notification arrives with your buddy's message still encrypted, and your device opens it and writes the notification itself. Right after your device restarts, before you first unlock it, or when the message can't be read, you get a general notification such as “New invitation” instead; open the notification bell on Home to see who it's from. If notifications never name anyone, update WitnessWork. Notifications can show on your lock screen; to hide what they say until you unlock, change the lock screen settings in your device's notification settings. To choose which Buddies notifications this device gets, use Buddies notifications, Ask to Join Alerts, and Badge Alerts in Buddies Settings, or change them for one buddy under Sharing & Alerts on their page. Everything still appears in the notification bell, and what you read or clear there is read or cleared on your other devices with Buddies too. On Android, Buddies notifications need Google Play services. If they stop arriving, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings (on Android, including its Buddies and Buddies news categories), then open Buddies to refresh. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.

entries.question: What's on a buddy's page, and can I rename them or change their color?

content.text: Open Buddies and tap a buddy; tap their photo to see it full size. Needs your answer lists their invitations you haven't answered; choose Going or Can't Make It there or in the Home notification bell. Together lists upcoming Plans and Follow-ups between you two, whoever invited whom, with each answer; tap a Plan to open its page, or use the menu on a buddy's invitation to change your answer. Next two weeks shows the days your buddy plans to go out next to your own; tap one of their days to plan the same time or ask to join. Invite to a Plan opens a new Plan with that buddy already invited, and View on Calendar opens Schedule. A nickname is a private name only you see; your buddy isn't told, and clearing it brings back their own name. Supporters can choose a buddy's color from the same swatches as the accent color, or any color with the eyedropper; Default brings back the color given when you paired, which everyone else keeps. Nicknames and colors are kept with your encrypted Buddies data, so they return when Buddies restores on another device. Nickname and color are right under their card, so you see a change as you make it. Sharing & Alerts opens their settings: what they see, whether their plans show on your calendar, and alerts. Their full schedule for the next eight weeks is on your calendar while Show on my calendar is on.

entries.question: Why are a buddy's plans or invitations missing or out of date?

content.text: Check that the request has been confirmed and Show on my calendar is on for that buddy. Your buddy may have paused sharing, or stopped sharing plans with you; WitnessWork doesn't say when they do. A buddy who shares only the time of day or no start time shows Morning, Afternoon, Evening, or Planned in place of a time. Calendar sharing covers only the next eight weeks. Both people need an internet connection to send and receive changes; open Buddies and pull down to refresh. Previously downloaded plans remain viewable offline, but new changes need a connection; Buddies says when you're offline, when it couldn't refresh, or when it can't verify this device. Seeing a buddy's calendar does not add their plans to yours. Turn on Buddies notifications in Buddies Settings and your device's notification settings, and check the Home notification bell for invitations even if no notification arrived. On Android, Buddies notifications need Google Play services; without them, changes still arrive when you open WitnessWork. The bell checks for new Buddies activity when you open it and when you return to WitnessWork; if it says it couldn't check, reconnect and tap Try Again.

entries.question: Why does my answer say Sending in or Not sent yet, or my request say Waiting to Send?

content.text: Going is sent to your buddy right away. Can't Make It waits 15 seconds first, in case you tapped it by mistake: tap Change to fix it before it's sent. Leaving the app sends it right away. Not sent yet or Waiting to Send means your answer or Ask to Join request hasn't reached your buddy, usually because you're offline or Buddies is temporarily unavailable. You don't need to answer or ask again: it's saved on this device and sends automatically the next time Buddies refreshes, such as when you open Buddies or return to WitnessWork while connected. While WitnessWork is open, it tries once more on its own shortly after. To send it sooner, reconnect and tap Try Again beside Your answer on the Plan or Follow-up, or open Buddies and pull down to refresh. Your buddy won't see the answer or request until it's sent.

entries.question: How do I hide a buddy, stop sharing, or delete my Buddies data?

content.text: Open a buddy's page, tap Sharing & Alerts, and turn off Show on my calendar to hide their plans on your calendar on all your devices with Buddies; sharing continues, and your own Plans with them still show. Remove Buddy ends the connection for both people, and reconnecting takes a new invite. They are not notified, though they may notice. If removal is pending while offline, they may still see your last shared plans until WitnessWork reconnects and completes it. Buddies Settings → Delete My Buddies Data removes all connections and invites and erases your encrypted Buddies data and encryption identity. It cannot be undone; reconnect and retry if deletion is pending. Your personal service records and contacts remain.

entries.question: Why does Buddies say it's been turned off for me?

content.text: WitnessWork can turn off Buddies for someone after a report of abuse, such as harassing a buddy. While it's off, Buddies can't sync, send invites, or share Plans. A Plan or Follow-up you invite buddies to then isn't sent, now or later: the app tells you, and the Plan shows Not sent beside them (change it once Buddies is back on to send it). You can still remove buddies and delete your Buddies data (Buddies Settings → Delete My Buddies Data). Your buddies aren't notified. WitnessWork knows you only by an anonymous account number your device made, with no name, email, or phone number, and can't read anything you share with buddies. If you think this is a mistake, contact support under Still need help?, using the support button in this screen's header, and include your app version. If the report was wrong, we turn Buddies back on.

entries.question: What is my WitnessWork account?

content.text: Your WitnessWork account is anonymous: there's no email, phone number, or password. Your phone makes a secret account key the first time you use Buddies, Scribe AI, or Backup, or view your recovery key, and WitnessWork's server knows you only by a random account number. Find it in Settings → Account. If the status there says Offline, this device has no internet connection; if it says Not responding, WitnessWork's server didn't answer, so tap Try Again in a few minutes. Either way, everything on this device still works, and the status checks again when the connection comes back. Each device proves it's the genuine WitnessWork app when it connects to your account (see "Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?"). The key stays on your devices: in iCloud Keychain on iPhone and iPad, and in Google's Block Store backup on Android. Buddies uses it for your identity, and the server never sees your name or anything you share with buddies. Your service records, contacts, and notes stay on your device; if you turn on Backup in Settings → Account, the server also keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy that only your devices can read.

entries.question: How do I move to a new phone or switch between iPhone and Android?

content.text: Use Set Up Another Device. It works between any two phones, including from iPhone to Android and back. On your old phone, go to Settings → Account → Set Up Another Device to show a QR code. On the new phone, install WitnessWork and choose Sign In with QR Code: during setup, tap "I already use WitnessWork", then From your other phone; after setup, it's in Settings → Account. Both phones show the same six-digit code. Check that they match, then tap Allow on the old phone. Both phones need the internet, and a code expires after 10 minutes. Your account and your buddies move to the new phone, and your old phone stays signed in. If the new phone used Buddies with another account, it asks first: that account's buddies stay on its other signed-in devices, or are removed for good if this was its last one. To bring your service records, contacts, and notes too, use Cloud Sync, which works between iPhone and Android: once it's on for the new phone, your records arrive without a restore step. Or turn on Backup in Settings → Account on the old phone first: the new phone then offers to restore them. iCloud Sync and Google Drive Sync work between phones of the same kind, and a backup file from Settings → Backup & Restore works between any two. The account travels end-to-end encrypted, so the server can't read it, and it keeps nothing once the new phone has it.

entries.question: What if signing in with a QR code doesn't work?

content.text: Make a new code on your old phone (Make a New Code) and scan it again. Each code works once and only for 10 minutes. Check that both phones are connected to the internet. If the connection drops after you tap Allow, keep both phones on the screen: the new phone shows Try Again and also continues by itself when it's back online. If the old phone says your account wasn't sent, check its connection and tap Allow again. Both phones need WitnessWork from the App Store or Google Play: a device that can't be verified can't use your account (see "Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?"). If the codes on the two phones don't match, tap Don't Allow and start over, since another phone may have scanned your code. If the new phone can't scan, check that WitnessWork may use its camera in your phone's settings. If you no longer have your old phone, use your recovery key instead: on the new phone, go to Settings → Account → Use a Recovery Key. If it still doesn't work, contact support from the Help Center; never send your recovery key.

entries.question: Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?

content.text: Your account, Buddies, Backup, Set Up Another Device, and Scribe AI work only in the genuine WitnessWork app. When a device first connects to your account, and again about every 90 days, WitnessWork asks Apple (App Attest, on iPhone and iPad) or Google (Play Integrity, on Android) to confirm the app and device are genuine. Apple and Google receive only that check, never your records, your account number, or your account key. Simulators, emulators, rooted devices, custom system software, and modified or unofficial copies of the app can't be verified; on Android the device also needs the Google Play Store and Google Play services, up to date. If Settings → Account says Not verified yet, Apple or Google couldn't be reached just then: wait a few minutes and tap Try Again. If it says Can't verify this device, reinstall WitnessWork from the App Store or Google Play and update the device's system software, then tap Try Again. Everything else in WitnessWork works on that device as usual, and your data stays on it. If a genuine device still can't be verified, contact support from the Help Center.

entries.question: What is my recovery key, and how do I keep it safe?

content.text: Your recovery key is your account key written out as WW1- and eleven groups of five letters and numbers. To see it, go to Settings → Account → Show Recovery Key; your phone asks for Face ID, Touch ID, your passcode, or your screen lock first when one is set. Copy it into a password manager, or share it to a private note or print it, and keep it somewhere only you can reach. Anyone who has it has your account, including your Buddies, so don't send it to other people or post it. If you lose it, view it again on any phone that still uses your account. If you think someone else has it, delete your Buddies data (Buddies Settings → Delete My Buddies Data): that removes your buddies and gives you a new account and recovery key. If you lose every phone and the key, no one can recover the account, including us.

entries.question: How do I use my recovery key on a new phone?

content.text: If you still have your old phone, Set Up Another Device is easier: see "How do I move to a new phone or switch between iPhone and Android?". Otherwise, install WitnessWork on the new phone, go to Settings → Account → Use a Recovery Key, and enter your key. It works between iPhone and Android. Case, spaces, and dashes don't matter, and the app tells you when a character is mistyped. If that phone already used Buddies with a different account, the app asks you first, and its Buddies data is deleted from the phone. While other devices are still signed in to that account, its buddies stay on them; on the account's last device, its buddies are removed for good. On iPhone and iPad, the key also replaces the account on your other Apple devices that use the same iCloud Keychain. The recovery key brings your account and Buddies identity. If your account has a backup (Settings → Account → Backup), the app then offers to restore your service records, contacts, and notes; otherwise Cloud Sync brings them over once it's on for the new phone (Settings → Device Sync), or you can move them with iCloud Sync, Google Drive Sync, or Settings → Backup & Restore.

entries.question: How do I see which devices use my account?

content.text: Go to Settings → Account → Signed-In Devices. It lists every device signed in to your WitnessWork account and when each was last active, with "This device" marked. Tap another device to sign it out, for example a phone you sold or lost. Signing out ends that device's connection, but if WitnessWork on it still has your account, it signs back in the next time it's used. If you think someone else has your account, delete your Buddies data (Buddies Settings → Delete My Buddies Data) to get a new account and recovery key, then set up your other devices again. Settings → Account → Account Activity shows your account's history for the last 400 days: sign-ins and sign-outs, devices signed out from another device, your account sent to a new phone, backups deleted or downloaded, Buddies set up or its data deleted, and suspensions. "Signed out … to protect your account" means a device's sign-in was used again after it had been replaced, which can mean someone copied it; check Signed-In Devices for anything you don't recognize. Device names are encrypted so only your devices can read them, and WitnessWork's server doesn't keep locations, IP addresses, or anything you share. Both need the internet, and they appear once your account is set up.

entries.question: How do badges work, and where do I find them?

content.text: Badges celebrate steady habits in your ministry, like sharing each month, sending your report, and going back to see people. There's nothing to set up: WitnessWork checks your records and adds a badge when you reach one. To see yours, tap your profile picture, then Profile. Your badges sit right under your profile card; tap one to see it up close, or tap See all to open Badges, where you can see every badge you have and what helps each one grow next. Most badges grow through four levels: Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Pearl. A few one-time badges, like First Bible Study, stay hidden until you have them. When something you just did earns a badge, like logging time, checking off that you shared, saving a visit or plan, sending your report, answering Going, or confirming a buddy, a small card with the badge slides in at the top of the screen. Tap it to celebrate the badge full screen, or swipe it away. Several new badges stack, newest in front; tap the ones behind to spread them out. A badge you don't tap, and one that arrives another way, such as a plan's day arriving overnight, time logged on your watch or another device, or a buddy's reply, doesn't interrupt you: it waits in the notification bell on Home. Tap View there to celebrate it, or X to dismiss it; either way the badge is saved and stays marked new on your profile until you open your badges. (Before version 1.45.0, a badge you just earned was celebrated full screen right away, and one that arrived another way showed a New badge card at the top of Home.) If your records already reach badges the first time WitnessWork checks them on a device, a one-time “Your badges are here” screen says how many you have: Take a look opens your profile, and Later closes it. It waits for a time you open WitnessWork without an update's tour. Badges reached by records you add or restore while setting up WitnessWork are added without it. Either way, your badges are already saved. Badges work on iOS and Android and update a moment after your records change and whenever you return to WitnessWork. They aren't the red number on the app icon, which counts unread items in the notification bell.

entries.question: How do I see a badge up close or share it?

content.text: Tap any badge, on your profile, on the Badges screen, or on a buddy's page in Buddies, and it opens full screen: the badge, its level, what it counts, and when you earned it. “Found in your history” means older records reached it and the month isn't known. Under your own badges, a line like “Next: Pearl · 41 of 60 months” shows how far that badge is from its next level, or “All four levels collected” once you have Pearl; tap the info button beside it to see what helps it grow. A level you haven't reached yet shows “Not yet” and how to get there, and so does a level a buddy hasn't reached when you tap it under See all on their page. Tap the badge to spin it. To share one, take a screenshot: the screen shows your name, as in “Anna's badge,” and WitnessWork at the bottom, and nothing is sent anywhere on its own. Your name comes from your profile, in Settings → Profile; without a name, the screen leaves it off. Close the badge with the X, by swiping down, or with Back on Android. With Buddies, your buddies' reactions appear under your own badge, and a buddy's badge lets you send one; see the question about what buddies see.

entries.question: Why do badges count months instead of hours?

content.text: So everyone grows at the same pace, whatever their circumstances. Every badge counts calendar months, never hours or goals. A month counts once, whether you shared for a few minutes or all day, and whether you mark that you shared or log hours as a pioneer. Badges never reset or depend on an unbroken run of months, so time off for illness, travel, or a hard season takes nothing away; the next month you share simply counts. Your streak is separate and never affects your badges. Year Round counts service years with at least 10 months of sharing, so two months off in a service year never count against you. Because each month counts only once, the highest level, Pearl, takes years. That's on purpose.

entries.question: What does each badge count, and why didn't a month count?

content.text: Sharing the Good News counts months where you logged time or marked that you shared. Year Round counts service years with at least 10 of those months. Reports Sent counts months whose report you sent from WitnessWork or marked as already sent. Ready to Go counts months with a Plan, once the Plan's day arrives. Kind Words counts months with a visit where you talked with someone; Not at Home visits don't count. Return Visits counts months you went back to someone you had visited before. Next Time counts months with a Follow-up that has a topic. Keeping in Touch counts the most different months you've talked with one person, in person, by phone, or by letter. Two by Two counts months a buddy went with you on a Plan or Follow-up, and shows only where Buddies is available. If a month didn't count: hours carried over by the rollover option don't count on their own, visits that came with a contact someone shared with you are theirs and don't count, a Plan counts only once its day arrives, and Two by Two needs a buddy who answered Going. One-time badges mark a first: your first Bible study, and your first buddy.

entries.question: What do my buddies see, how do reactions work, and how do I stop sharing badges or badge alerts?

content.text: Your buddies see the badges you have, each at its highest level, in a row on your page in Buddies. See all there shows each collection with the levels you've reached and the ones still ahead, plus your one-time badges. They never see your progress, counts, or dates. In data protection mode, First Bible Study isn't shared. To stop sharing badges, turn off Badges in Buddies Settings. When a buddy gets a new badge, you get an alert with their name and the badge, like “Levi earned a badge” with “Year Round, Silver” below it; tap it to open their page. You get at most one alert per buddy a day, and later badges that day arrive quietly in the notification bell. Badges found in imported or restored history, and one-time badges, aren't announced. To encourage a buddy, open their page in Buddies, tap one of their badges, and pick a reaction: 🎉, 🎊, 🔥, 👏, 👍, or 🙌. You can react to each badge once; picking another reaction replaces the first. Only that buddy sees who reacted, and nothing else is sent: no message, and none of your own badges. If you're offline, your reaction is sent when you're back online. When a buddy reacts to one of your badges, you get an alert like “Anna reacted 🔥 to your badge,” at most once per buddy a day, and the reaction appears in the notification bell and when you open that badge. To stop alerts for new badges and reactions on a device, turn off Badge Alerts in Buddies Settings; both still appear in the notification bell. With Show badges off, you can't react, and reactions to your badges aren't shown.

entries.question: Where do my buddies' new badges and reactions show up?

content.text: In the notification bell on Home, under From your buddies, below anything waiting for your answer. A buddy's new badge shows the badge with six reactions: 🎉, 🎊, 🔥, 👏, 👍, and 🙌. Tap one to encourage them right away. After that, the row shows what you sent; tap Change to pick another. Tap the row or its badge to see the badge full screen, marked New if you hadn't seen it yet. Several badges from one buddy within a day share one row. When a buddy reacts to one of your badges, tap it to open your badge with every buddy's reaction. Buddies' news never adds to the red number on the bell or the app icon; a small dot on the bell means something new from your buddies. It says only Today, This week, or Earlier, never the time. Dismiss it with X or Clear All, or let it clear on its own after 30 days. It shows only for your current buddies, wherever Buddies is available, on iPhone, iPad, and Android, and only while Show badges is on. To stop the alerts but keep the news in the bell, turn off Badge Alerts in Buddies Settings. If you're offline, your reaction is saved and sent when you're back online. When you get a new badge yourself and share badges with your buddies, the New badge card says who will see it, like “Ben and Grace will see it.” To stop sharing badges, turn off Badges in Buddies Settings.

entries.question: Can I lose my badges, move them to a new device, or hide them?

content.text: Badges are keepsakes: once you have one, it stays, even if you later delete the time, visits, or plans behind it, or a buddy leaves. Progress toward the next level is kept too when data protection mode suggests deleting old details. Your badges sync between your devices when sync is on and are included in backup files, so restoring a backup on a new phone brings them back. When imported or restored history reaches new badges, they're added quietly with one summary instead of a celebration for each, or with no summary at all when you import or restore while setting up WitnessWork. To hide badges, open Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges and turn off Show badges. That hides them everywhere, including from your buddies and celebrations, without forgetting them; turn it back on and they return.

entries.question: How do I track mileage?

content.text: Mileage Tracking is optional and available for every publisher type. Answer Yes on the "Track mileage?" card on Home, or turn on Track Mileage in Settings → Profile. Then add your first car; only a name is required. Log a trip with Log Trip on Home's Mileage card, from the Add button, or on the Mileage screen. Enter the distance (turn on Round Trip to double it) or switch to Odometer and enter start and end readings. Odometer Start fills in from that car's last reading. Tap a trip to see its details, or long-press it to edit, log it again today, share, or delete it.

entries.question: How is the estimated fuel cost calculated, and what happens when fuel prices change?

content.text: Estimated fuel cost is distance ÷ the car's fuel economy × its fuel's price, using the values in effect on each trip's date.
