It only appears once the car has a fuel economy and its fuel has a price; trips without both are left out and the report says so. A fuel's price is shared by every car that uses that fuel. When you change a price or a car's fuel economy, choose From a Date to apply it from that day forward (earlier trips keep the old value) or Fix Current Value to correct a mistake, which also updates the past trips that used it. Each fuel and car keeps a history; long-press an entry to delete it. The amount is only an estimate. If you're reimbursed, the actual amount is calculated by whoever reimburses you.

entries.question: Can I use kilometers, litres, or L/100 km?

content.text: Yes. Open Mileage → Settings (the gear) → Units. Distance can be miles or kilometers, and fuel economy can be mpg (US), mpg (UK), L/100 km, or km/L. Auto follows your device's region. Fuel is priced per gallon with mpg (US) and per litre with every other choice. Currency follows your device's region. Changing units only changes how numbers are shown; your trips aren't altered.

entries.question: How do I share or export my mileage report?

content.text: Open Mileage, choose Day, Week, Month, or Year (service year, September to August), and use the arrows or swipe to pick the period. Tap the share button at the top to Copy the report, Share it as text, or Export CSV for a spreadsheet. The text lists totals, per-car totals when you have more than one car, and each trip except in the Year view. The CSV has one row per trip with the car, odometer readings, distance, note, fuel, fuel economy, price, and estimated cost. Trip notes are included, so check them before sending. To share one trip, open it and tap the share button.

entries.question: What's the difference between archiving and deleting a car?

content.text: Open Mileage → Settings, tap the car, and choose Archive or Delete…. Archiving hides the car from new trips but keeps its trips in your reports; unarchive it anytime from Archived Cars. Deleting removes the car and all of its trips on every device that syncs with this one, and can't be undone. Deleting a fuel removes its price history, so cars using it stop showing an estimated cost.

entries.question: What does the chart on the Mileage screen show?

content.text: Open the Mileage screen and choose Week, Month, or Year. The chart shows how far you drove each day, or each month of the service year (September through August). When more than one car has trips in that period, each bar is split by car, using the colors next to each car's total. Tap a bar to open that day or month and see its trips. The Day view has no chart, and a period without trips shows none. Bars show distance, not estimated cost.

entries.question: Does my mileage sync, and does it work on Android?

content.text: Mileage works on iOS and Android. Cars, fuels, prices, and trips sync between your devices with Device Sync, a Supporter feature, using the option you choose in Settings → Device Sync: Cloud Sync, which also syncs between iPhone and Android, or iCloud (Google Drive on Android). They're included in WitnessWork Backup (Settings → Account) and in backups from Settings → Backup & Restore on both platforms. Mileage is never shared with Buddies and doesn't appear on your calendar or Service Report.

entries.question: How do I turn mileage tracking on or off?

content.text: Use the Track Mileage switch in Settings → Profile. Turning it off hides the Home card, the Log Trip action, and the Mileage screen, but keeps your trips; turn it back on and everything returns. If you chose No Thanks on the Home card, this switch turns it on anytime. To erase your mileage, open Mileage → Settings → Delete All Mileage Data. This deletes it on every device that syncs with this one and can't be undone. You can also hide only the Home card with Settings → Preferences → Home Screen.

entries.question: How do I get a pet, and how do I turn it off?

content.text: The Pet Companion is optional and works on iOS and Android. On Home, the Meet your companion card offers one: tap Choose a pet (or tap one of the animals on the card to start with it chosen), pick a lion cub, pup, kitten, donkey, or lamb (the pup and the kitten come in several coats), give it a name if you like, and tap Adopt. A short intro then shows how its hearts fill, how your streak opens up hats and room items, and how to decorate; tap Next through it, or close it to skip it. If you chose Not now, bring the offer back with Add Sections while editing Home (press and hold an empty space on Home), or turn on Pet in Settings → Preferences → Home Screen. To hide the pet, long-press its card, choose Edit Home Screen, and tap the gray minus on it, or turn off Pet in Settings → Preferences → Home Screen. Hiding keeps your pet, its room, and its keepsakes; turn Pet back on and everything returns. You have one companion at a time.

entries.question: How do my pet’s hearts work?

content.text: A new pet starts with 3 of 5 hearts, or 4 if you were active the day before you adopted it. Each day you're active in the ministry adds one heart, up to 5. A day counts when you log time (including marking that you shared in the ministry, even with 0 minutes), save a visit (a conversation, return visit, or not-at-home), or make a new plan (editing a plan doesn't count). Visits that came with a contact someone shared with you are theirs, so they don't count. One heart a day, however much you did; hours don't matter. When 10 days pass without an active day, your pet loses half a heart every 3 days. At half a heart it falls asleep, and after 60 days without an active day it dies (it's shown greyed and lying down). Kingdom Publishers go by the month instead, as they report: an active day fills all 5 hearts (a pet adopted in a month you've already been active starts with all 5), and they stay full through the next month, so marking once a month that you shared keeps your pet happy. If a whole month passes without an active day, its hearts start fading 10 days into the month after, as above, and an active day fills them right back up. Tap a sleeping pet (or, if it died, Tap to wake) to wake it with 1 heart; the next active day adds hearts again. Patting it (tap it, or drag across it to rub) is just for fun and never adds hearts. Hearts are worked out from your records each time, so they're the same on every device and come back if you restore a backup.

entries.question: What does the lamp in the room mean?

content.text: The lamp is your Service Streak. It burns brighter as your streak grows, from unlit at 0 to its brightest once your streak reaches 30. For Kingdom Publishers the streak counts months, so it is brightest at 12. If you turned off Show streak in Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges, the lamp keeps a steady medium glow and no streak number shows anywhere.

entries.question: How do I decorate my pet’s room?

content.text: Tap your pet's card on Home anywhere except on your pet (tapping your pet pats it), or long-press the card's name and choose Hat & Room…. Pick a tab (Hat, Wall, Floor, Bed, Shelf, Light, Sign, or Window) and tap a picture; the room at the top changes right away and the change is saved. Live window follows your clock and the season where you are (from your region; seasons are reversed south of the equator); turn it off to choose a time of day and a season, each of which can also stay Live. The sign on the wall can show your hours this month, your hours this service year, the months you shared in the ministry, your next plan, or this month's conversations and return visits, or nothing. Some items are open from the start. Each of the others opens up the first time your streak reaches the number on its flame: from 1 to 120 kept planned days for pioneers and other roles that log hours, or from 1 to 12 months in a row for publishers. Hats follow their own numbers (see the question about hats). Once an item opens up, it stays open, even if your streak ends later. If you turned off Show streak in Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges, or you log hours but haven't made any plans, one more item opens up instead for each month you're active (any day with logged time, a visit, or a saved plan) since you adopted your pet, in a set order, and a locked item shows the month it opens up. Items that are already open stay open either way. Some items are secrets, which follow neither your streak nor the months; see the question about secret items. When something you just did opens up an item or a hat, a small card with it slides in at the top of the screen (from version 1.45.0): tap it to see the item in your pet's room, then Try it on or Decorate Room to come here, or swipe the card away. An item that opens up while WitnessWork isn't open, or whose card you don't tap, waits in the notification bell on Home; opening Hat & Room clears it.

entries.question: How do I get hats for my pet?

content.text: Your pet can wear a hat, or none: 12 to start working toward, and secret hats you find along the way (see the question about secret items). Tap your pet's card on Home anywhere except on your pet, pick the Hat tab, and tap a hat; it's saved right away, and your pet wears it on Home, in its details, in shared pictures, and in the Home Screen widget (iPhone and iPad). The 12 open up with your streak like room items, on their own numbers: the first three come quickly, at 3, 5, and 9 kept planned days (or in your first month for publishers), and the rest take longer, up to 120 days (or 12 months). If you turned off Show streak, or you log hours but haven't made any plans, the first three open up in your first active month and the rest one month at a time. A locked hat shows the number or month it opens up at, and once a hat opens up it stays open. Your pet takes its hat off while it rolls over or lies down. Your buddies see your pet without its hat.

entries.question: What are the secret hats and room items?

content.text: Besides the hats and room items that open up with your streak, every tab but Window and Sign has secret ones. Until you find one, it shows only as a dark shadow with a question mark and ??? for its name, and tapping it says only that it's a surprise. Each secret opens up on its own milestone as you keep going in the ministry and care for your pet; which one is part of the surprise. None depend on hours, none need a buddy, and none can be missed for good, so you can find any of them later. The first time you see one after it opens up, it says New; then pick it like any other item. Secrets you've found stay open, sync with your pet like other items, and come back from a backup. If a secret you expected hasn't shown up, open your pet's details again after your records sync; secrets are worked out on each device from what's stored there.

entries.question: Can I change or rename my pet?

content.text: Yes. Tap your pet's card on Home (anywhere except on your pet) to open its details, then tap Rename or Change pet; or long-press the card's name for Rename… and Change Pet…. Rename lets you type a name of up to 20 characters; clear it and save to use the animal's name instead. Change pet picks another animal or coat for the same companion: it keeps its name, hearts, hat, room, and keepsakes. Names are yours and are never translated.

entries.question: How do I share a picture of my pet?

content.text: Tap your pet's card on Home (anywhere except on your pet) and tap Share (the share button at the top right), or long-press the card's name and choose Share…. Its share card shows your pet in its room with its name and hearts, a few facts (your Service Streak while it's above 0, unless you turned off Show streak in Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges; how many days you've been together; and how many hats it has opened up), and the WitnessWork name at the bottom. Tap Share to send the card as a picture with any app in the share sheet. Nothing is sent until you choose where it goes, and the picture holds nothing else about you or your records. If sharing fails, a message says so; try again, and if it keeps failing, close and reopen WitnessWork.

entries.question: Why are other pets in my pet's room, and how do I hide them?

content.text: They're your buddies' pets, visiting for the day. When you use Buddies on iOS or Android, each buddy who shares their pet with you and is part of something you're doing today brings it to your pet's card on Home. That includes a Plan you invited them to or accepted from them, a Follow-up you added them to, or a buddy's Follow-up you're joining. A buddy who declined doesn't bring theirs. Each buddy's pet visits once, however many things you share with them today, and it leaves when the day ends. Visitors sit behind your pet, so yours and your lamp always stay in front.
To find out whose pet it is:
Tap your own pet. Once its hearts float away, each visitor says who it's visiting with.

Long-press a visiting pet to see View Plan (or View Follow-up), View your buddy, and Hide their pet. In a big crowd, a pet that's hidden behind others can't be long-pressed; use the list below instead.

Tap your pet's card (anywhere except on your pet) to open its details. The Visiting Today row says how many pets are visiting and with whom. Tap it for the full list, then tap a pet to open that Plan or Follow-up, or long-press it for the same menu.

To hide visitors, open your pet's details and tap the settings button at the top right. Turn off Buddies' pets visit to hide them all, or turn off a single buddy. The same switch, Their pets visit mine, is under Your Pet in Buddies Settings, and for a single buddy on their page under Sharing & Alerts. Choosing Hide in a visiting pet's menu does the same for that buddy, and the message that appears has an Undo button. These choices only change what you see. Buddies aren't told, and they still see your pet if you share it. To stop sharing your own pet, turn off Pet in Buddies Settings.

entries.question: Can I see my pet on my home screen?

content.text: On iPhone and iPad, yes. Long-press your home screen, tap the + button, search for WitnessWork, and choose Pet Companion. Small shows your pet; medium adds its name, hearts, your streak, and what its wall sign shows; large shows its whole room with its name and hearts. The widget moves through the day on its own, and opening WitnessWork refreshes it. Until you adopt a pet, it asks you to choose one in the app. Android doesn’t have WitnessWork home screen widgets.

entries.question: Does my pet sync, and what do my buddies see?

content.text: Your pet, its name, hat, room, the hats and room items it has opened up, and keepsakes sync between your devices with Device Sync, a Supporter feature, using the option you choose in Settings → Device Sync: Cloud Sync, which also syncs between iPhone and Android, or iCloud (Google Drive on Android). They're included in WitnessWork Backup (Settings → Account) and in backups from Settings → Backup & Restore too. Its hearts aren't stored: each device works them out from your records. With Buddies, your pet's kind, coat, and name are shared (not its hat) with your buddies, end-to-end encrypted. To stop sharing them, turn off Pet in Buddies Settings; the switch shows once you have a pet. Nothing else about your pet, and none of your records, is shared.

entries.question: Can I recover my buddies on another device or from a backup?

content.text: On iPhone and iPad, your Buddies encryption key is kept in iCloud Keychain, so your buddies follow you to your other devices signed in to the same Apple Account with iCloud Keychain on (Passwords, in iCloud settings), and come back after you reinstall WitnessWork. With sync on, Buddies starts by itself on your other devices once they sync: your buddies, your answers to invitations, the notifications you've read or cleared, and the nicknames and colors you chose show on each one, and each device gets Buddies notifications (choose which in Buddies Settings on that device). Without sync, open Buddies on the other device and pull down to refresh. Each device then shares the plans it has, so turn on sync to keep what your buddies see the same. Your buddies see one name for you from all your devices: the one you last changed in Profile on a device using Buddies. Buddies Settings shows it under How buddies see you. On Android, Google Play services keeps the key: it comes back when you reinstall WitnessWork on the same phone while Google backup is on (Settings → Google → Backup), and with a screen lock set it's also saved, end-to-end encrypted, in your Google backup, so it can return when you set up a new phone from that backup. Without a screen lock, the key stays on that phone. Android devices don't share one key the way iCloud Keychain does, so each Android device, and an iPhone and an Android phone, have their own Buddies connections. Regular WitnessWork backup files do not contain the encryption key. If the key is unavailable, or you used Delete My Buddies Data, reconnect with new invites. A device whose key went missing can still delete the Buddies data it kept, or sign in to another account; buddies of the old key keep that connection until they remove it. Keep your personal records backed up separately.

entries.question: How do I see how many hours I have left this month or year?

content.text: Open the Progress tab from the bottom bar. The Month sub-screen shows time so far and hours left for the current month. Pioneers can switch to the Year sub-screen to see annual goal progress, time so far, remaining hours, and a per-month breakdown comparing actual hours to plan.

entries.question: How can I tell if I'm ahead or behind on my hour goal?

content.text: Open the Progress tab from the bottom bar. On the Month view, the report shows how much is left and how many days are left, and the line under it shows whether you're ahead or behind your plans. The Daily Pace card shows how much a day it takes to reach your goal; add it with Edit Cards if it isn't there. Pioneers can switch to the Year view, where the Service Year Pace chart shows how far ahead or behind your Annual Goal you are today, and each month's bar shows how that month did against its goal. The Year Pace card shows how much a month you need for the rest of the service year.

entries.question: How much do I need each day to reach my goal?

content.text: Add the Daily Pace card on the Progress tab's Month view (tap Edit Cards, then Add Cards); it's there by default for roles with a monthly goal. It takes what's left of your monthly goal and divides it by the days left in the month after today, the same count the month's report shows as days left. For example, with 25 of 50 hours done and 20 days left, it shows 1.3 hours a day (the figure rounds up slightly, so keeping to it is always enough). On the last day of the month, it shows everything that's left as today's amount. Make the card wide to also see about how much that is a week. Credit time counts up to its monthly limit, as on your report, and your plans aren't counted; the Projected Month card shows where your plans put you. Once you reach your goal, the card says so. For a past month it shows what you averaged a day, and for a future month what each day would need. It doesn't appear when the month has no goal. For the year, the Year Pace card does the same with your annual goal, spread over the months left in the service year.

entries.question: How do I read the Service Year Pace chart?

content.text: Open the Progress tab and switch to Year. If your status has an Annual Goal, such as regular pioneer, the Service Year Pace card appears below your milestones. The dashed gray line is where your Annual Goal puts you by the end of each month. It is built from each month's own goal, so a mid-year appointment or an auxiliary pioneer month changes it, but a Monthly Goal you changed yourself does not. The green line is your time so far, counted the same way as your Service Report, including each month's credit limit. The dashed green line adds the time you have planned. The faint line is last service year, shown when you logged time in it, and the number at its end is last year's total. If a line runs well past your Annual Goal, the space above the goal is drawn on a compressed (logarithmic) scale so the months below stay readable. Press and hold the chart, then slide your finger, to see any month's totals. "Ahead of pace" compares your time with where the goal line is today. Below the card, each month has a bar: solid for logged time, lighter for credit time, and striped for plans, with a tick at that month's goal. The key above the months explains these marks, and the Hours and vs Goal columns give the numbers. Every bar uses the same scale, so you can compare months. Without an Annual Goal you see the month bars but not the chart. If a month looks wrong, press and hold it to change its status or goal. The chart is drawn on your device from your own entries and isn't shared.

entries.question: Can I display time as "1h 30m" instead of "1.5"?

content.text: Yes. Open Settings → Preferences → Region & Formats and choose a Duration Format. Both formats are available everywhere time is shown.

entries.question: Can I start the week on Monday instead of Sunday?

content.text: Yes. Settings → Preferences → Region & Formats → Start of Week lets you choose the first day of the week. The change applies to the calendar, schedule, and any other weekly views.

entries.question: Can I force dark mode or light mode?

content.text: Yes. Open Settings → Personalization → Color Scheme and pick Device, Dark, or Light. The app will stop following your phone's setting and use the one you choose.

entries.question: Does WitnessWork support Bold Text, larger text, and other display settings?

content.text: Yes. WitnessWork follows your device's display settings; there's nothing to turn on in the app. Text size: it uses the size you choose (Larger Text on iPhone and iPad, Font size on Android), up to the largest accessibility sizes, and wraps or stacks rows so words stay whole; on a tablet, very large text swaps the sidebar for the bottom bar. Bold Text on iPhone and iPad, and Bold text on Android 12 or later, make WitnessWork's text heavier too; on Android, the change shows when you come back to WitnessWork. Reduce Transparency (iPhone and iPad) makes blurred headers and bars solid. Increase Contrast (iPhone and iPad) makes gray text and borders stand out more, in light and dark mode; on Android, High contrast text is applied by the system. Reduce Motion (Remove animations on Android) skips confetti and keeps celebrations still. To choose light or dark mode, use Settings → Personalization → Color Scheme. These settings change only how WitnessWork looks, never your records. If text is cut off or hard to read, report it from the Help Center with a screenshot, your device, and your text size; cover names and addresses first.

entries.question: Can I change the app's icon?

content.text: Alternate app icons are a Supporter perk on iOS. Open Settings → Personalization → App Icon and choose an alternate. Alternate app icons are unavailable on Android.

entries.question: How do I rearrange or hide the sections on Home?

content.text: Press and hold a section, then choose Edit Home Screen, or press and hold an empty space on Home. The sections start to jiggle. Hold a section and drag it to move it; on iPad, sections can move between the two columns. Tap the gray minus at a section's top corner to hide it (tap Undo if you didn't mean to). To show a hidden section again, tap Add Sections at the top; it comes back first on Home. Tap Done, or tap an empty space, when you're finished; on Android, the back button works too. A section with nothing to show right now, like Approaching Conversations when you have no follow-ups today, appears as an outline while you edit, so you can still move or hide it. Getting Started stays at the top until you finish or close it. Some sections depend on your role or device: Timer appears for roles that log time, Mileage when mileage tracking is on, and Service Year Summary on iPad with an annual goal. With Reduce Motion on, sections stay still while you edit. You can also show, hide, and reorder sections in Settings → Preferences → Home Screen. Hiding a section never deletes your data. Your layout is a preference, so it's included in backups and syncs with your other devices when sync is on.

entries.question: How do I choose what's on my Progress screen?

content.text: Each tab on Progress (Month, Year, and All-time) has its own cards under its summary, and you choose them separately. To change a tab's cards, press and hold any card; it lifts and the cards start to jiggle, and you can drag it straight away. You can also tap Edit Cards under your cards, or the grid button at the top. While the cards jiggle, drag a card to move it, tap the gray minus at its top corner to remove it (tap Undo if you didn't mean to), and drag the curved handle at its bottom corner to make it small or wide; tapping the handle switches sizes too. Cards that come in only one size have no handle. Tap Add Cards at the top to see every card that tab offers. Month has Daily Pace, Studies, Days Out, Visits, Credit, Weeks, Projected Month, Service Year, Year Pace, Streak, Lifetime, and Days. Year has Service Year Pace, Needed a Month, Average, Best Month, Last Year, Days Out, Months Out, Studies, and Visits for the service year shown. All-time has Best Year, Average, Best Month, Days Out, Months Out, Studies, and Visits across all your records. The Days list on Month can show every day of the month or, when compact, only the latest few in a short list that scrolls on its own; drag its handle down or up to switch. To lift the Days list, hold its title rather than a day, since each day has its own menu. Tap Done, or tap the summary at the top, when you're finished. Each tab's summary (the month's report, the service year's total, or your lifetime hours) and the lists of months and years always stay. Some cards only appear when they apply: Daily Pace and Projected Month need a monthly goal, Year Pace, Service Year Pace, and Needed a Month need an annual goal, Credit needs a role whose report counts hours, hour cards on Year need a role that logs hours, Streak needs streaks turned on, and Mileage needs mileage tracking. With Reduce Motion on, the cards stay still while you edit. Removing a card never deletes your time or reports. Your cards are a preference, so they're included in backups and sync with your other devices when sync is on. To start over on a tab, tap Edit Cards there, then Reset Cards.

entries.question: What do the Year and All-time cards count?

content.text: On Year, time counts as each month's report counts it: credit time counts up to that month's limit. Average on Year runs from your first month with time to the last month that's ended; the month under way joins only while it's the only one. Last Year compares this service year so far with last service year at the same point, or the whole of both once the year is over. On All-time, time counts as you logged it, before monthly credit limits, the same as your lifetime hours and Year by Year. Average on All-time covers the service years that have ended, or the one under way if it's your first. Months Out counts the months you shared in the ministry, with or without hours, starting from your first record; the month under way counts once you've shared in it, and it's never shown as missed. On All-time it also shows your longest run of months in a row. Studies counts each contact you marked a Bible study with once, and shows the most any one month had, which is that month's figure for your report. Contacts you've deleted aren't counted. Visits counts visits where you talked with someone; not-at-homes are counted separately. Visits that came with a contact someone shared with you are theirs, so Studies and Visits leave them out. Everything is worked out on this device from your own records, and nothing new is stored or shared. If a figure looks wrong, check the month's report and the visits on the contact; you can contact support from the Help Center, leaving out names and notes.

entries.question: Can I change the order of the tabs?

content.text: Yes. Open Settings → Preferences → Tab Order and use the up and down arrows beside each tab, or long-press a tab's name to move it to the top or bottom. The new order applies right away to the bottom bar on phones and the sidebar on tablets, on iOS and Android. Tabs can be reordered but not hidden. WitnessWork still opens on Home, and Progress only appears for roles that log hours; it keeps its place in your order if you change roles. On iPad, Command-number keyboard shortcuts follow your order too. The order is a preference, so it's included in backups and syncs with your other devices when sync is on; it doesn't change any of your records. To go back, move the tabs back to Home, Contacts, Progress, Schedule. If the order doesn't update, restart the app and use Still need help? below.

entries.question: Why was my timer rounded to the nearest 5 minutes?

content.text: That was old behavior. Recent versions save the exact stopwatch time when you stop the timer, with no rounding. If you're still seeing 5-minute rounding, update the app to the latest version.

entries.question: Can I add notes to a time entry?

content.text: Yes. When you add or edit a time entry, you can attach a note (e.g. "cart witnessing" or "cut short"). You can also tag entries with categories so similar entries stay grouped in your time reports.

entries.question: I'm a special pioneer, why is the app showing me an annual goal?

content.text: Special pioneers don't have an annual goal by default. If yours appears, open Settings → Profile and set Annual Goal to No. Your monthly goal stays in place and the annual bar on the Progress tab's Year sub-screen will be hidden.

entries.question: Are LDC and other credit hours included in my totals?

content.text: Yes. Credit hours count toward your monthly hour total. For the service-year total, up to 55 credit hours per month are counted, in line with the branch's published cap. Anything above the cap is still kept on the entry but doesn't roll into the annual total.

entries.question: Will my entries, plans, or reminders move if I travel to another time zone?

content.text: Entries and plans stay on their day. As of the April 2026 update, every time entry and plan is anchored to its calendar date independent of time zone, so traveling or crossing a daylight-saving boundary won't move them to a different day. A Plan's time stays on the clock too: a 10:00 AM Plan reads 10:00 AM on the day clocks change. Older entries created before that update are migrated automatically the first time you open the new version. When you open WitnessWork after changing time zones, Home, Schedule, and Progress switch to the new zone's today, and reminders set for a time of day, such as a Plan's reminder or the reminders to log time, plan next week, or submit your report, move to that same time where you are. Follow-ups keep their exact moment, so they show at the matching local time. If you ever spot an entry on the wrong day, please send a bug report and we'll take a look.

entries.question: How do I plan across months or see my whole service year?

content.text: The Schedule tab has two views; switch between them with the buttons at the top. Month shows your weeks as one calendar you scroll through without stopping at the end of a month, so you can plan this month and next side by side. The month you're reading stays bright and the others fade back, and the card above the calendar shows that month's goal: logged and planned time (striped) against your goal, the time you've logged, and whether you're ahead of or behind your plans. Tap it for goal coverage, schedule pace, and the Assistant. Each day shows the time you planned, or the time you logged once you log some. Tap a day to see or change it, or touch and hold it to add time or plan it. Year shows the twelve months of the service year (September through August), each day colored like the calendar, under the same card for the whole service year: logged and planned time (striped) against your annual goal if you have one, the time you've logged, and whether you're ahead of or behind your plans. Tap a month, or pinch outward, to zoom into it; pinch inward in Month to zoom back out. A labeled line marks where one service year ends and the next begins; tap it to see that year. Use the arrows or swipe to change years, and tap Today to come back. Both views only show what's already in your records; changing views doesn't share anything.

entries.question: What's on a Plan's page, and how do I change a Plan?

content.text: Tap a day on the Schedule tab, then tap one of its Plans, or tap a Plan on Home, to open it. Its page shows the date, when it starts and ends (with the next day's date if it runs past midnight) or Anytime for a Plan with no set time, how long it is, its Type, how often it repeats, the place, and the note; tap the place to open it in Maps. To change the Plan, tap Edit (the pencil). For a recurring plan, saving asks whether the change is for only this date, this and future dates, or all dates. More (•••) holds Duplicate, Log as Time, Open in Maps, Copy Address, Copy Note, and Delete. Duplicate opens a new Plan with the same details; a one-time Plan's copy starts on the same day next week, and you can change the date before you save. With Buddies, the page also lists who you invited and how each answered, plus anyone who asked to join, with Invite. Tap Invite Buddies to invite someone right away while the Plan is still ahead; they get the date, time, title, location, and note. To take someone off, use Edit. For a Plan you joined through a buddy's invitation, the page shows who organized it and your answer. Switch between Going and Can't Make It anytime until the Plan ends: Can't Make It takes the Plan off your schedule, and Going puts it back. After the Plan, you can still open it, with its note and photos, for a month, but no longer change your answer.

entries.question: Can I plan hours without picking a time?

content.text: Yes. On the Plan form, tap the How long? button next to the date. Choose Just hours to plan the hours for that day without a time, or Time span to pick when you start and finish; the hours add up for you. New Plans open in whichever one you used last, so your usual way is ready next time. A Just hours Plan shows Anytime on your Schedule and counts toward your goals like any other Plan. With Notify Me on, it reminds you at 8:00 AM that day instead of before a start time. Buddies you invite see the day and how long, with no time. To give it a time later, edit the Plan and switch to Time span. If another of your devices still runs an older version of WitnessWork, it shows the Plan at noon until it updates.

entries.question: Can I edit or delete a single occurrence of a recurring plan?

content.text: Yes. On the Schedule tab, tap the day, then tap the plan to open it. To change only that date, tap Edit (the pencil), make your changes, save, and choose Only this date. Changing the Type, title, location, or Notify Me reminder for one date turns that date into its own one-time plan. To remove only that date, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan. Your recurring plan stays intact for every other day.

entries.question: How do I mark a day I'm not going out without breaking my recurring plan?

content.text: Tap a plan on that day in the Schedule tab to open it, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan. Do this for each plan on that day. Only that day is removed, and a recurring plan keeps going from the next day forward. To go out at a different time that day instead, tap Edit, change it, and choose Only this date when you save.

entries.question: Can I plan more than one activity on the same day?

content.text: Yes. A day can hold as many plans as you like, one-time, recurring, or both, like field service every Friday morning and a Bible study every Friday evening. Every plan on a day adds up: the day's planned time on the Schedule calendar, the time left to plan, and your projected total all count each one. To add another plan, tap the day on the Schedule tab, then tap + next to Plans. To skip a recurring plan on one day, open it, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan; your other days stay the same. To change it for one day only, tap Edit and choose Only this date when you save. One-time plans used to replace a day's recurring plans. When you updated, days where that happened were set to skip the recurring plan, so your totals didn't change. If a day shows more time than you expect, tap it and delete the plan you don't need. Plans stay on your device, sync between your devices if you turned sync on, and only their day, time, and length are shared with your buddies if you use Buddies.

entries.question: Can WitnessWork plan my month for me?

content.text: Yes. During setup, if you log hours and have a monthly goal, you get a quick preview of the Assistant: pick the days you usually go out and it spreads your goal across those days for this month, or next month if fewer than seven days are left. This month's plan starts on the 1st, so the days that have already passed get plans too: log the time you already spent on them. Days you've already logged time on are left alone. Tap any day to change its plan with the slider, or to plan a day yourself. Tap Add to my schedule to save them as plans on the Schedule tab, where you can change or delete any of them, or tap I'll plan later to continue without plans. The weekdays you didn't pick become off days, so the Assistant won't suggest plans on them; change this anytime in Settings → Preferences → Plans → Availability. After setup, you plan on the Schedule tab by tapping any day, and the Assistant there suggests plans whenever you're short of your goal. Plans are saved with your other records and don't count toward your report; log the time you actually spend. Kingdom Publishers who don't log hours, and anyone without a monthly goal, skip this step but can still add plans from the Schedule tab.

entries.question: Can WitnessWork remind me to log time for a day I planned?

content.text: Yes. Go to Preferences → Plans, turn on Remind Me to Log Time, and choose a Remind At time (8:00 PM unless you change it). If a day has a plan but no time logged, you get one reminder at that time after the day's plans end: a morning plan reminds you that evening, and a plan still going at your Remind At time reminds you the next day. Several plans on the same day give one reminder, and when two days' reminders would arrive at the same time they're combined. Logging any time for that day stops its reminder and clears one you've already received; removing that day's plans or turning the setting off does too. A day planned with no time doesn't remind you, and days you missed before turning the setting on aren't included. Tapping the reminder opens Add Time with the date, planned time, and type already filled in. The reminder is also listed in the Home bell for a week, even if system notifications are off. The setting appears when you track hours; Regular Publishers turn on Log my hours first. Turning it on asks for notification permission, or opens your device settings if you've declined before. Reminders are worked out on your device from your own plans and time and aren't sent anywhere. Each device schedules its own reminders up to two weeks ahead, so open WitnessWork at least every two weeks to keep them coming. If you log time on another device, open WitnessWork on this one so it can cancel that day's reminder. On Android, the system may deliver a reminder a few minutes late to save battery. If reminders don't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings (on Android, including its Reminders category) and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.

entries.question: Can WitnessWork remind me to plan next week?

content.text: Yes. Go to Preferences → Plans, turn on Remind Me to Plan Next Week, then choose Remind On and Remind At (Saturday at 6:00 PM unless you change them). At that time, if the following week has no plans yet, you get one reminder inviting you to plan it. Weeks follow your Start of Week setting. Any plan in that week, including a recurring plan, means no reminder, and adding one later clears a reminder you've already received. If you've marked every day as an off day under Availability, you aren't reminded. Tapping the reminder opens the Schedule at that week's month, where you can tap a day to plan it or use the Assistant's suggestions when you have an hour goal. The reminder is also listed in the Home bell until that week ends, even if system notifications are off. It's available for every publisher role. Turning it on asks for notification permission, or opens your device settings if you've declined before. Reminders are worked out on your device from your own plans and aren't sent anywhere. Each device schedules up to two weeks ahead, so open WitnessWork at least every two weeks to keep them coming, and if you plan on another device, open WitnessWork on this one so it can cancel the reminder. On Android, the system may deliver a reminder a few minutes late to save battery. If reminders don't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings (on Android, including its Reminders category) and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.

entries.question: How do streaks work?

content.text: Your streak counts how consistently you keep the plans you make. For pioneers and other roles that log hours, each planned day you log any time on adds one, even if you log less than you planned. Days without a plan don't add to it or end it, so plan the days you mean to go out. For publishers, each month you share in the ministry adds one, whether you mark the month on Home or log time. Your streak shows on Home's header and your Profile from its first day (before version 1.45.1, once it reached 3). Your pet's details show it too, even at 0; tap the info button beside it for what it counts. When logging a day takes it to a milestone, like 3, 5, or 10, a short celebration plays; other days, and growth that arrives another way, such as time logged on your watch or another device, make the flame on Home flare instead. When it's about to end, tap it on Home to log the day that's due. To hide your streak, turn off Show streak in Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges.

entries.question: When does my streak end, and how do I keep it?

content.text: A planned day can still be logged until the end of the next day. If that passes with no time logged for it, your streak ends. When yours is about to end, the flame on Home shows the time left, and a Streak Reminder comes at 6:00 PM on the last day. For publishers, a month can be recorded until the end of the next month, and the reminder comes three days before that month is over. If you can't go out on a planned day, remove that day's plans ahead of time: tap each one on Schedule, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan. For a recurring plan, only that date is removed. The day stays planned while any plan is left on it. If you went out but forgot to log it, add the time on that day and your streak comes back. Turn Streak Reminders off in Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges. They need notifications allowed for WitnessWork.

entries.question: Can my buddies see my streak?

content.text: Yes, from its first day, if you share it. (Before version 1.45.1, a streak showed once it reached 3, and buddies on those versions still see it only from 3.) Your buddies see the number on your card in their Buddies list, not your time or reports. It's end-to-end encrypted like the rest of what you share. To stop sharing it, open Buddies Settings and turn off Streak. A streak that ended stops showing on your buddies' phones even if your app hasn't opened since.

entries.question: Can I turn off streaks?

content.text: Yes. Open Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges and turn off Show streak. Your streak no longer shows on Home or your profile, nothing celebrates it, Streak Reminders stop, and Home's greeting no longer counts days in a row. Your buddies' streaks are hidden too, and yours stops being shared with them. Nothing is lost: your streak comes from your plans and the time you log, so turning Show streak back on shows it again right away, unless it ended in the meantime. The setting follows you to your other devices when sync is on. To hide badges as well, turn off Show badges on the same screen.

entries.question: How do I plan a route for my service day?

content.text: Route planning is a Supporter feature on iPhone, iPad, and Android. Open it from any day from today on: tap the day on Home or in Schedule (on iPad, the day's details show beside the calendar), then tap Plan Route; or touch and hold a day and choose Plan Route; or choose Plan Route in a plan's menu to plan the day around that plan. On Home, Plan Route also shows at the top of the conversations card when at least two of today's stops have a map location. A day with no follow-ups or plans can still be planned from scratch. Anyone can open it to see the day on the map; Shortest Order and Start Route need Supporter. The map shows your route with a card at each stop saying when you'd get there, and the box at the top shows when the day starts, when it finishes, and how long that is. Zoom in to see cards that would overlap, and drag the bar under the map to make it taller or shorter. On iPad and other wide screens the map sits beside the list. Use the arrows beside the date to plan another day. Stops start as the day's open follow-ups and plans that have an address or pin. Follow-ups already answered by a visit that day, and follow-ups for dismissed contacts, aren't included. Tap Add Stop to add Home, your Kingdom Hall, a place or address from search (you can also paste coordinates such as 37.7749, -122.4194 or a map link there), one of your contacts, or a pin you drop on the Map tab. From version 1.45.0, you can also pick contacts on the Contacts map, tapping their pins or drawing around them, and tap Plan Route to add them all at once. You can also touch and hold the route map to drop a pin and add it as a stop, the start, or the finish. A route can have up to 10 stops. To change the order, drag a stop by its grip, or touch and hold it and drag; you can also use Move Up and Move Down in the stop's ⋯ menu. Shortest Order asks the WitnessWork server for the fastest driving order; it needs an internet connection, works with up to 10 stops, and can be used 10 times in any 24 hours. Remove a stop from its menu; the day's stops you remove are listed below so you can add them back. Set how long you'll spend at each stop with its time chip. Between stops, the line shows the drive and, when you'd get somewhere early, how long you'd wait. From version 1.45.0, the map follows the roads, and drive times come from Apple Maps on iPhone and iPad, or from HERE through the WitnessWork server on Android, with traffic as it is when you plan; without a connection, they're estimated from the distance between stops. Either way, check them against fixed appointments. A stop shows when you'd be late for its set time. With Start Visits at Set Times on (in Details, when a stop has a set time), arriving early waits until the set time; turn it off to see how early you'd get there. In Details, link the route to one of the day's plans, invite buddies, and add notes with formatting, lists, and links. Your route is saved on this device for that day and isn't synced to your other devices. Tap Start Over to rebuild it from the day's follow-ups and plans. Planning a route never changes your contacts, follow-ups, or plans. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support option and keep householder details out of public reports.

entries.question: How do I choose where my route starts and finishes, or save Home and my Kingdom Hall?

content.text: At the top of the route, tap the place under Start to choose your current location, the first stop, Home, your Kingdom Hall, one of the day's plans that has a place, or any place you search for, and tap the time to change when you leave. If a plan with a place starts before your first follow-up, such as a meeting for field service, the route starts there at that time. At the bottom, tap the place under Finish to end at the last stop (the default), go back to where you started, or finish at Home, your Kingdom Hall, or any place you search for. The finish isn't a stop, so there's no time spent there; the drive to it is added, and the finish time is when you'd get there. Start Route takes your navigation app on to the finish. Shortest Order puts the stops in order from the start and keeps the finish last. To save Home or your Kingdom Hall, tap Set Home or Set Kingdom Hall in the Start or Finish menu, or in Add Stop, then search for the address or drop a pin on the Map tab. After that, they're one tap away in those menus and in Add Stop. To change or remove one, touch and hold it in Add Stop. Saved places stay on this device and aren't synced.

entries.question: How do I plan a route with buddies?

content.text: Invitations go out with a plan, so a route's buddies are its plan's buddies. In the route's Details, tap Invite Buddies. If the route already belongs to one of the day's one-time plans, the row opens to your buddies: tap one to invite them to that plan right away, and tap them again to take them off, which cancels their invitation. If the route doesn't have a plan yet, Invite Buddies opens a new plan filled in from the route's day, start time, and starting place; choose who to invite there and save, and the route then belongs to that plan. Buddies get the plan's date, time, title, location, and note, plus any changes you make to the plan, and they can say whether they're going; their answers show in Details. They don't get the route's stops, order, or notes. You can also start from the plan: choose Plan Route in its menu to plan the day around it. Plans that follow a buddy's invitation are invited to by their organizer, and recurring plans can't carry invitations, so Invite Buddies doesn't show for them. Buddies must be set up first: with no buddies yet, Invite Buddies opens Buddies.

entries.question: How does my route open in Apple Maps, Google Maps, or Waze?

content.text: Tap Start Route. Your route opens in the Default Navigation App chosen in Settings → Preferences → Navigation, in the order shown, starting with the place you chose as the start when it isn't your current location, and ending where you chose to finish when that isn't the last stop. Google Maps opens the whole route as one trip with every stop in order. Apple Maps does the same on iOS 18.4 or later; on earlier versions it opens one stop at a time. Waze always opens one stop at a time because its links accept only a single destination. When stops open one at a time, come back to WitnessWork and tap Navigate to Stop 2 (and so on) for the next stop. To go to any one stop, open its menu and tap Navigate Here. If Google Maps isn't installed, the route opens in a web browser, which may show fewer stops; install the app or choose another navigation app. On Android, choose Google Maps or Waze. If a map app doesn't open, check that it's installed and try again.

entries.question: What's shared when I plan a route?

content.text: To find the order, WitnessWork sends the map coordinates of your starting point and each stop to the WitnessWork server, which passes only those coordinates to HERE, a mapping service, to calculate the drive. Names, addresses, notes, topics, and visit details are never sent. The request also carries the app's random account identifier, the one tied to your Supporter purchase, so the server can confirm Supporter status and count your routes; it isn't sent to HERE. The server doesn't store coordinates. It keeps only the times of your route requests from the last 24 hours to apply the daily limit. From version 1.45.0, to draw the route along the roads and time each drive, WitnessWork also asks for driving directions between your start, each stop, and your finish whenever the route changes. On iPhone and iPad, Apple Maps receives those coordinates, as when you get directions in Maps. On Android, they go to the WitnessWork server, which passes only the coordinates to HERE; the request carries your anonymous WitnessWork account so the server can count requests, and the server doesn't store the coordinates. When you open the route, your navigation app receives each stop's address, or its coordinates for a pin you placed, and the place you finish when it isn't the last stop, just as it does when you navigate to a single contact. Usage analytics record counts such as how many stops a route had, never locations. The route you build, including its notes, added stops, and where it starts and finishes, is saved only on this device; it isn't sent anywhere or synced. So are the addresses you save as Home and Kingdom Hall. Buddies you invite get the route's plan, the same as inviting them from the plan: its date, time, title, location, and note. They don't get the route, its stops, or its notes.

entries.question: Can I import contacts from my phone's address book?

content.text: Not at this time. Contacts are entered manually in WitnessWork. This keeps your ministry contacts private and avoids accidentally pulling in personal contacts.

entries.question: Can I import data from MyTime, Ministry Assistant, or another app?

content.text: MyTime backups are supported. In MyTime, go to More → Settings → Backup and email yourself a backup, then save the attached .mytimedb file on your device. On Android, send it from MyTime on your iPhone and download the attachment on your Android phone. Open Settings → Import Data → From MyTime, or choose From MyTime during setup, choose that file, and review the preview before importing. Other apps' backup formats are not automatically supported. If you can export readable text, paste it into Scribe AI and review what it adds. Review its proposed records and warnings before saving. WitnessWork JSON backups belong in Settings → Backup & Restore instead. To bring in data from Notes or paper later, use Settings → Import Data.

entries.question: How do I back up and restore my data?

content.text: For an automatic, end-to-end encrypted backup, turn on Backup in Settings → Account; see "What is WitnessWork Backup?". For a backup file, open Settings → Backup & Restore → Create Backup or Restore From Backup to export or restore a JSON backup on iOS or Android. To restore, choose the witness-work-backup.json file you saved with Create Backup. On a new device, you can also choose From a backup file on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen; restoring there finishes setup with your restored profile. Backups include service records, plans, contacts, visits, categories, mileage, your pet, profile, and shared preferences. A restore replaces the included local data; older backups may omit categories or profile, which are kept as they are, and contacts in older backups keep their custom field values. A backup made with a newer version of WitnessWork can't be restored until you update WitnessWork on this device. If some items in a backup can't be read, the rest is restored and WitnessWork tells you how many items were left out. Device identity, sync settings, data protection mode, analytics consent, and onboarding progress stay local to this device. Photo files are not embedded in JSON backups. For iCloud or Google Drive photos, enable photo sync separately; Cloud Sync doesn't carry photos yet. A backup restores on iPhone or Android, so it can move your records from one to the other; to keep both in step instead, use Cloud Sync (see “What is Cloud Sync?”). Save a current backup before restoring and keep it in a private location; it can contain householder details. Use the Help Center’s private support option for recovery help.

entries.question: My backup looks unreadable or my restored records are missing. What should I do?

content.text: A WitnessWork backup is structured JSON for the app to read, so it does not look like a printable Service Report. Keep the original file unchanged and restore it through Settings → Backup & Restore → Restore From Backup. If records are missing, preserve the original backup and create a separate backup of the device's current data before trying another restore. Email support with the app version and what happened; arrange any file sharing privately. Backup files can contain contact details and notes, so keep them out of public bug reports.

entries.question: What is WitnessWork Backup?

content.text: WitnessWork Backup keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy of your service records, time, plans, contacts, visits and notes, categories, mileage, profile, and shared settings on WitnessWork's server, so you can restore them on a new phone, on iPhone or Android. It's free for everyone and off until you turn it on: go to Settings → Account and turn on Back Up to WitnessWork. It then backs up when your data changes, when you leave the app, and at least once a day; Back Up Now backs up right away. If Last Backup shows a problem instead of a date, the note under it says what to do: Waiting for connection goes on by itself once you're online, Update required clears once you update WitnessWork, Too large means your data is over 20 MB (save a backup file in Settings → Backup & Restore instead), and Too many devices means you need to delete another device's backup first. Settings → Account shows when it last backed up and lists one backup for each of your devices. Photos aren't included (contact photos and photos in notes), and neither are this phone's own settings like data protection mode, sync settings, or analytics consent. A backup can be up to 20 MB, and an account can keep backups from up to 8 devices. It works alongside Cloud Sync, iCloud Sync, and Google Drive Sync, which keep your devices in step; the backup is a snapshot for moving to a new phone, including between iPhone and Android, or recovering a lost one.

entries.question: Can WitnessWork read my backup?

content.text: No. Your phone encrypts the backup with a key made from your account key before it leaves the phone, and only your devices have that key. WitnessWork's server stores the encrypted backup, its size, when it was uploaded, and a random number for each device, never your name, email, or device name, and it can't read any of your records. That's also why no one can recover your backup for you: if you lose every phone that uses your account and your recovery key, your backup can't be opened by anyone, including us. Keep your recovery key somewhere safe (Settings → Account → Show Recovery Key).

entries.question: How do I restore my backup on a new phone?

content.text: Install WitnessWork on the new phone and bring your account over. With your old phone, use Set Up Another Device: during setup, tap "I already use WitnessWork", then From your other phone, and scan the code on the old phone (Settings → Account → Set Up Another Device). Without your old phone, use your recovery key: Settings → Account → Use a Recovery Key. The new phone then offers to restore your backup. When your other devices use Cloud Sync and are at least as up to date as the backup, your records arrive through Cloud Sync instead. If it has no records yet, tap Restore. If it already has records, choose Combine to keep them and add the backup's, or Replace to use only the backup. Restoring combines every device's backup on your account. You can also restore later from Settings → Account → Restore from Backup. A backup from a newer version of WitnessWork is left out until you update, and one that can't be read is skipped; the app tells you. When iCloud Keychain or Google's backup brings your account back on a reinstalled phone, the app offers your backup once. Afterwards, turn on Backup on the new phone too.

entries.question: How do I delete my backup, and how long is it kept?

content.text: Go to Settings → Account. Tap one device's backup to delete just that one, or tap Delete Backup to delete every device's backup; both also turn off backup on this phone, and they're gone from the server right away. Other devices with backup on back up again the next time they're opened, or within about 20 minutes while they're open. Turning off Back Up to WitnessWork asks whether to delete this phone's backup too. A device's backup that hasn't been updated for 400 days is deleted automatically. Delete My Buddies Data (Buddies Settings) also deletes your backup, because it gives you a new account and recovery key; with backup on, the next backup goes to your new account. If deleting fails because you're offline, nothing changes; try again when you're connected.

entries.question: What is Cloud Sync?

content.text: Cloud Sync keeps your records the same on all your devices, including between an iPhone and an Android phone. Each device that uses it keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy of its data on WitnessWork's server, and your other devices on Cloud Sync combine those copies, usually within seconds while the app is open. It's the default for devices that haven't chosen a sync option. Open Settings → Device Sync to see which option this device uses, turn sync off, or switch to iCloud (Google Drive on Android). A device syncs one way at a time, and only with your devices that use the same option. Photos don't sync with Cloud Sync yet; they stay on the device that added them. When Cloud Sync needs Supporter access, or WitnessWork has paused it for a while, Settings → Device Sync says so; your changes stay on this device and sync once it's back, and Sync now checks again. A new phone you set up from your account's QR code or recovery key gets your records through Cloud Sync without a restore step. If your newest backup is newer than every Cloud Sync copy, for example from a phone that stayed on iCloud, the new phone offers to restore it too.

entries.question: Is Cloud Sync more private than iCloud or Google Drive sync?

content.text: Cloud Sync is always end-to-end encrypted: each device's copy is encrypted on the device with a key only your devices have, so WitnessWork's server stores data it can't read. The server sees things like your anonymous account, how many of its devices sync, and the size and time of each copy, never what's in it. iCloud and Google Drive sync store a copy in your iCloud Drive or a hidden folder of your Google Drive. Apple and Google protect it, and Apple encrypts it end to end if you turned on Advanced Data Protection, but WitnessWork doesn't encrypt iCloud or Google Drive sync end to end itself. If you lose every device and your recovery key, Cloud Sync's copies can't be read by anyone, including us.

entries.question: How do I switch between Cloud Sync and iCloud or Google Drive?

content.text: Open Settings → Device Sync and choose Cloud Sync, iCloud (Google Drive on Android), or Off. Switching keeps everything on this device and combines it with your devices on the new option; nothing is replaced, and nothing deleted on your other devices comes back. Leaving Cloud Sync removes this device's copy from WitnessWork's server; your other devices on Cloud Sync keep what they've already synced from it. Leaving iCloud or Google Drive leaves this device's last copy there, and your other devices keep syncing with each other but not with this one. A device that already used iCloud or Google Drive before Cloud Sync keeps it, and Settings offers the switch once. To sync all your devices together, choose the same option on each.

entries.question: My devices are not syncing. What can I check?

content.text: First check Settings → Device Sync: devices sync only with your devices that use the same option (Cloud Sync, iCloud, or Google Drive), so choose the same one on each. With Cloud Sync, keep the app open on both devices and check your internet connection; Sync now retries at once. If it says Cloud Sync is paused, nothing is wrong on your side: changes wait on this device and sync when it's back. For iCloud: on iOS, use the same Apple Account, turn on iCloud Drive, and enable WitnessWork under iCloud on each device. On Android, see “Google Drive Sync isn’t working on my Android device. What can I check?” iCloud sync requires Supporter access. Open Settings → Device Sync and use Sync now. Changes waiting to be sent are retried; an unreadable file or newer app version is shown in the status, so update every device and try again. The status shows Uploading to iCloud until Apple confirms the upload, and Last synced counts only confirmed uploads. If your iCloud storage is full, changes stay on this device; free up space or upgrade your storage in Settings → [Your Name] → iCloud and uploading resumes on its own. Keep an exported backup and the device containing your latest data. Rebuild iCloud data replaces the iCloud data with this device’s data and removes iCloud photos it doesn’t use. Your other devices switch to that data the next time they sync, replacing changes made on them before then, and the Home bell notes it. Update WitnessWork on every device first: an older version keeps its own data until it is updated. Contact private support from the Help Center if syncing remains incomplete. Keep householder details out of public reports.

entries.question: Why are contact photos missing on my other device?

content.text: Photo sync is an optional Supporter feature on iOS and Android for devices that sync with iCloud (Google Drive on Android). Open Settings → Device Sync and turn on Include images in sync. Photos don't sync with Cloud Sync yet; they stay on the device that added them. This uploads profile and contact photos to your private iCloud container (or WitnessWork's hidden Google Drive folder) and downloads referenced photos; they count against your iCloud or Google storage. Update WitnessWork on every device to use photo revisions safely. Pausing photo sync on one device keeps the uploaded files and local copies. To remove uploaded photos, choose Remove iCloud photos and pause photo sync on other devices first, or they can upload their copies again. Removing a contact or its photo removes downloaded copies when that change arrives; obsolete cloud copies are cleaned up after a one-day grace period. If a photo is missing, keep the device with the original, check storage and permissions, then use Sync now. Use the Help Center’s private support option if it still fails; do not include householder information in public reports.

entries.question: What happens to setup choices, deleted contacts, and reminders during sync?

content.text: Restart onboarding affects only this device. Choosing Set up fresh pauses iCloud sync until you explicitly enable it in Settings; then choose Merge both or Restore from iCloud as appropriate. Restore from iCloud reads other devices’ snapshots and replaces local data after confirmation. During onboarding, a device that already has records asks before replacing them, and Supporters can choose Merge instead. Keep this device’s data makes your other devices switch to this device’s data the next time they sync, replacing changes made on them before then. Restoring data does not send Buddies declines for plans absent from the backup. Recoverable deleted contact details are retained for up to 90 days, then removed while deletion evidence remains. Reminders are rebuilt on this device after merges and restores, keeping the reminder time chosen for each follow-up and plan; notification permission is required and only future reminders are scheduled. For recovery, keep the device with the latest records and export a backup before replacing data. Use private Help Center support if you need help.

entries.question: How do I remove an old device from sync?

content.text: Each device that uses iCloud Sync keeps its own copy of your data in your iCloud, and that copy stays after you stop using the device, even after a reinstall or a new phone. Remove it when you no longer use a device, for example one you sold, replaced, or reset. On a device that still syncs, open Settings → Device Sync → Devices and tap Remove beside the old device. Devices not synced in 90 or more days are marked. Removing deletes only that device’s copy from iCloud, including details it still held of contacts deleted elsewhere. This device keeps everything it has already synced, and your other devices aren’t changed. If the removed device is still in use, it adds its data back the next time it syncs; turn off iCloud Sync on it first if you want it to stop. Before removing a device, this device must finish syncing its data; if asked, go back, tap Sync now, and fix any problem the status shows. If the device uses a newer version of WitnessWork, update this device first. Devices replaced by Rebuild iCloud data can be removed at any time. Photos aren’t stored per device, so removing a device doesn’t remove photos; use Remove iCloud photos for that. Devices is part of Settings → Device Sync on every option, all Supporter features: with iCloud the copies are in your iCloud, with Google Drive on Android in your Google Drive, and with Cloud Sync, removing a device deletes its copy from WitnessWork's server. If you need help, use the Help Center’s private support option and keep householder details out of public reports.

entries.question: How do I use Scribe AI?

content.text: On Home, tap the glowing microphone in Quick Actions, or tap + and choose Speak an update. Say what you did or plan to do, like “Two hours this morning, and I talked with John at 42 Oak St, follow up next Tuesday,” then tap Done. To type instead, tap the keyboard at the top of the screen while it listens. You can also scan handwritten notes on iPhone and iPad, or read photos of paper pages; check the text before you send it. Scribe AI shows what it understood as cards: time, plans, and contacts with their visits and follow-ups. Uncheck anything you don’t want, pick the right person when it asks something like “Which Maria?”, and tap Add. Nothing is added until you do. Tap an added contact or plan to open it. Right after, Undo in the message at the bottom of the screen takes it back, and for 30 days you can open the conversation from History (the clock in Scribe AI) and tap Undo there. If Quick Actions isn’t on Home, hold any Home section, tap Edit Home Screen, and add it back.

entries.question: What can Scribe AI do?

content.text: Scribe AI can log time, including in a category such as LDC or a new one you name, change or delete time you logged, create Day Plans and change their date, start time or length, add contacts and update their name, phone, email or address, and log visits with follow-ups. It can also answer questions about your time this month or service year, your plans, your contacts and visits, and the plans your buddies share with you. Everything it would change appears as cards for you to review first. Apart from time you logged, it can’t delete anything, change your settings, create or change Recurring Plans, invite buddies, or send anything to anyone. When you plan with a buddy, the plan’s card reminds you to invite them once it’s added. If a visit note reads like instructions to an AI, Scribe AI may skip it and say it couldn’t read it.

entries.question: How do Scribe AI limits work?

content.text: Scribe AI usage depends on how much it reads and writes, not on how many messages you send. A quick update uses a little; long conversations and paper pages use more. To see how much of each limit you’ve used, as a percentage, and when it resets, tap the percentage at the top of Scribe AI or open Settings → Scribe AI → Usage. Without Supporter, you have a monthly limit that starts with your first use and resets 30 days later. Supporters get much higher limits: a session limit that resets 5 hours after it starts, and a weekly limit that resets 7 days after it starts. If your Supporter subscription ends, the monthly limit applies again, counting what you’ve already used in it. When you reach a limit, Scribe AI tells you when you can use it again, and anything it was already working on still finishes. You can always add time, contacts and plans yourself. Reading paper pages counts toward the same limits, and you can read a limited number of pages in any 24 hours.

entries.question: What does Scribe AI send, and what’s kept?

content.text: Your voice is turned into text on your device; recordings are never saved or uploaded. When you send a message, Scribe AI sends the conversation’s text and only the details it needs to understand it, such as today’s date, your goal, your upcoming plans and your contacts’ names, plus anything it looks up while answering. It goes over an encrypted connection through OpenRouter to a model host under a Zero Data Retention arrangement, so it isn’t stored or used for training. It carries a code made from your account that can’t be traced back to you, so the host’s safety checks apply only to you. WitnessWork’s server doesn’t keep your messages; it records only how much you used. Your conversations stay on this device and aren’t synced or backed up: it keeps your 50 most recent conversations, each for 90 days after you last used it. The records you add sync like any others. Photos of paper pages are resized on your device, with their location and other details removed, and read the same way; the app deletes its copy of each page once it’s read or you skip it, or when you close Scribe AI or start a new conversation. Your original photos stay in your library. With data protection mode on, Scribe AI doesn’t send your contact list or visit notes. Find the OpenRouter ZDR policy in Settings → About.

entries.question: Why can’t I speak to Scribe AI?

content.text: Scribe AI turns speech into text only on your device, so voice needs on-device speech recognition for your app language. The first time you speak in a language, Scribe AI may wait while your device downloads that language’s speech model. On Android, voice needs Android 12 or later with on-device speech recognition for your language. Where it isn’t available, Scribe AI opens with the keyboard instead, so you can type. Voice also needs microphone access: if you turned it off, turn on Microphone for WitnessWork in your device’s Settings. If another app is using the microphone, close it and try again. If a call or switching apps stops a recording, what Scribe AI heard waits in the message box so you can finish it and tap Send.

entries.question: Scribe AI got something wrong. What do I do?

content.text: Before you tap Add, uncheck any card you don’t want, or tap Say a change (or type) to tell Scribe AI what to fix, like “Make that Saturday at ten.” It replaces the cards with new ones. After you tap Add, tap Undo in the message that appears, or for up to 30 days open the conversation from History in Scribe AI and tap Undo there. Undo removes what was added and puts back what was changed or deleted, except a change you’ve edited again since, or a contact or type that something else now uses; Scribe AI says how many stayed. You can also edit any record yourself as usual. If Scribe AI keeps getting something wrong, email support from Still need help? in the Help Center, and describe what happened without sharing personal details.

entries.question: What does Scribe AI remember about me?

content.text: Scribe AI keeps short notes about how you work, so you don’t have to repeat yourself. When you correct it (“No, the build is what I call LDC”), use your own word for something, mention a lasting preference, or say “Remember…”, it quietly saves a short note, and every new conversation starts with these notes. To forget one, say “Forget what I said about the build.”

To see, edit, or add notes yourself, go to Settings → Scribe AI → Memory. Write one note per line. Memory holds up to 1,500 characters; when it’s full, a note has to be shortened or removed before another can be saved, and you can make room yourself. Turn off Memory on the same screen to stop Scribe AI from reading or saving notes, or tap Clear memory to erase them all.

Your notes stay on this device. They aren’t synced or backed up. They’re sent along with each conversation, the same way as the rest of your messages, so they’re never stored or used for training. Scribe AI doesn’t save personal details about the people you visit, or anything it reads in your visit notes. A change you make in Settings applies from your next conversation.

entries.question: Does Scribe AI work offline?

content.text: No. Scribe AI needs an internet connection to understand what you say. While you’re offline, its button shows a no-internet badge, and tapping it explains why. You can still add time, contacts and plans yourself, and Scribe AI works again as soon as you’re back online. If the connection drops while Scribe AI is answering, it picks up again by itself when you’re back online, unless you’ve typed or sent something since; then tap Try again. If it drops while reading photos of paper pages, Scribe AI keeps the pages it hasn’t read: once you’re back online, tap Try again in the message box to read just those pages without choosing the photos again, or Skip unread pages to keep only what was read.

entries.question: What happened to Notes Import and Import Credits?

content.text: Notes Import is now part of Scribe AI. You can still type or paste notes, scan them on iPhone and iPad, or read photos of paper pages, and Scribe AI turns them into cards to review. Import Credits are gone: usage limits that reset on a schedule replace them (see How do Scribe AI limits work?). Imports you added before can still be undone for up to a year: open Scribe AI, tap History, and find them under Earlier imports.

entries.question: MyTime Import says the file is not a database. What should I use?

content.text: MyTime Import needs an original .mytimedb backup created by MyTime. A PDF, text export, WitnessWork JSON backup, or a file renamed to .mytimedb will not work. To get one, go to More → Settings → Backup in MyTime and email yourself a backup, then save the attached file on your device and select it through Settings → Import Data → From MyTime. Keep the original file unchanged. If a valid backup still fails, email support privately with the error and app version; do not post the backup in a public issue.

entries.question: How do I send my report to Hourglass or NW Publisher?

content.text: Open the month's Service Report, choose Hourglass or NW Publisher in the dropdown above Submit, and tap Submit. Review and send the report in the destination app. Copy and Share are also available. NW Publisher accepts only the previous month's report. Hourglass receives preaching time separately, with Credit Time included in the default report comment; if you replace the comment, check that it still says what you need. Update WitnessWork if a submission option is missing.

entries.question: How do I quickly log a visit?
