content.text: Tap + and choose Log Visit, then pick the person. On iPad, Log Visit… is also in the menu bar's File menu. Without searching, the list starts with Nearby (contacts within about 250 m of you, closest first), then Follow-ups Due (today's and missed ones from the last 30 days), then Recent (visited in the last 2 weeks), then All Contacts A–Z. Type to search; if the person isn't there, tap Add as a new contact to create them and log the visit next. After you pick someone, tap Had a Conversation to add notes and a follow-up in the visit form, or Not at Home to log it right away, with Undo at the bottom of the screen for a few seconds. On a contact's page, + Add → Not at Home logs it the same way. In data protection mode, Not at Home isn't offered and the visit form opens directly. Nearby is optional: it appears only if you allow location, and you're never asked unless you tap Turn On. Your location is used on this device only to sort the list; it isn't saved or sent anywhere. If Nearby is missing, check that location is allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings and that the contact has a location on the map. Touch and hold a person to open their contact instead.

entries.question: How do I see a conversation and its follow-up, or bring a buddy along?

content.text: Tap a conversation in a contact's Conversation History, the Up Next card on a contact, or a person on Home's conversations card, and it opens in a sheet without leaving where you are. Tapping a follow-up reminder opens it there too. Across the top is who it was with: tap them to open the contact, or use Call, Text, and Navigate. Below, a line runs from what happened ("You talked with…", when, your note, and its fields) to the follow-up, with a Today marker in between, so you can see at a glance whether the return visit is ahead or behind. The follow-up says when you're going back and how far off it is, the topic, who's going, and the reminder. Log Visit appears once its day comes, and Reschedule while it's still open. A missed follow-up turns amber, one you kept links to the visit that kept it, and a dismissed one can be planned again. With no follow-up, the sheet links to your next visit with that person, or offers Plan the next visit after the latest one. Tap the pencil to edit, or ••• to reschedule, copy the note or topic, dismiss the follow-up, or delete the conversation; deleting can't be undone. If you use Buddies, invited buddies and their answers show inside the follow-up. While it's still ahead, the dashed + invites someone right away and shares only its date and time, the householder's first name, the address, and the topic. To take someone off, edit the conversation. Follow-up invitations are unavailable in Data Protection Mode. Opening a conversation changes nothing, and only inviting a buddy shares anything. If something looks wrong, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.

entries.question: How do I use the Today's Conversations card on Home?

content.text: The card shows the follow-ups you scheduled for today. From 5 PM it shows Upcoming Conversations, which adds tomorrow's; those can be rescheduled but not logged until their day. Swipe sideways to move between people. When you've been, tap Talked to log the conversation in the visit form, or tap Not at Home to log the attempt right away. Undo appears below the card for a few seconds after Not at Home. The calendar button reschedules the follow-up. Tap a person to see that conversation and its follow-up in a sheet. Use the ••• button or touch and hold a person for call, message, directions, Open Contact, and Dismiss Follow-Up. A follow-up counts as done once you log any visit with that person on or after its day. The bar at the top fills as you go, and the card shows All caught up when every one is done. Tap Done, or touch and hold the title and choose Close for Now, to hide the card until you add or reschedule a follow-up. A follow-up still open 4 hours after its time moves to missed follow-ups in the notifications tray. Not at Home is unavailable while data protection mode is on. Visits are saved like any other visit on this device. To remove the card for good, touch and hold its title, choose Edit Home Screen, and tap the minus on the card. Add Sections brings it back while you edit Home. If something looks wrong, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.

entries.question: Can I keep visit notes without scheduling a return visit or reminder?

content.text: Yes. When adding or editing a visit, turn off Follow Up and save. The visit and its notes remain, but that visit has no scheduled follow-up or reminder and will not appear as overdue. You can turn Follow Up on later and choose a date and time. To stop an older follow-up reminder, edit that visit and turn Follow Up off.

entries.question: Can I track extra details on a conversation, like the publication I used?

content.text: Yes. Open Preferences → Conversation Fields, or tap Add Custom Fields on the conversation form, and add a field such as Publication. Field names can be up to 14 characters. Every field appears on the form for conversations and Not at Home visits; leave it empty when it doesn't apply. Saved values show on that visit in the contact's history. When you tap a field, values you've entered in it before appear as suggestions, most used first, and narrow as you type; tap one to fill it in. Below each field, Earlier visits lists what you entered there on that contact's previous visits, such as publications or videos you already shared, so you can choose something new. You can rename and reorder fields any time without losing what you entered. Archiving a field hides it but keeps its values. Delete it from the Archived list to remove the field and its values from every conversation for good. Fields and values stay on your device, are included in backups, and sync between your devices when sync is on; update WitnessWork on each device to see them there. They aren't included when you share a contact. Contact fields are managed separately in Preferences → Contact Fields. With data protection mode on, don't record religion, health, family situation, language, or ethnicity. If a field is missing from the form, check whether it was archived. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.

entries.question: Can I save a contact filter and switch to it quickly?

content.text: Yes, with saved views, free on iOS and Android. In Contacts, tap the Sort & Filter button (the sliders) at the top, choose filters and a sort, then tap Save as view at the top and name it (up to 30 characters), such as Bible studies or Spanish territory. Your views appear as buttons under the search field, above the last-visit chips, and at the top of the map: tap one to show it, and tap it again to return to your own filters. A view applies to the list and the map alike. Search text isn't saved in a view. While a view is showing, changes you make in Sort & Filter or with the last-visit chips are marked Edited; tap Update view to keep them, Save as new view to keep both, or Reset to discard them. To reorder your views, touch one, pause briefly, then drag it along the row. Touch and hold a view without moving to rename or delete it, or choose ••• → Edit Saved Views to rename, reorder, and delete views. Deleting a view never changes your contacts. Renaming or archiving a contact field keeps views working; if you permanently delete a field, filters on it are ignored. Views are stored on your device, included in backups, and sync between your devices when sync is on; update WitnessWork on each device to see them there. Which view is showing stays on each device. If a view shows unexpected contacts, open Sort & Filter to check its filters, or tap Reset to undo unsaved changes. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.

entries.question: What does the Suggested sort in Contacts do?

content.text: Suggested is the Contacts list's default sort on iOS and Android. When you aren't searching, the list starts with up to four short sections: Nearby (contacts within about 250 m of you, closest first, with their street), Follow-ups Due (follow-ups due today or missed in the last 30 days, most overdue first), Recent (contacts visited in the last 2 weeks), and Been a While (people you last talked with 3 weeks to 4 months ago who have no follow-up planned, Bible studies first, then favorites, with when you last talked). A Not at Home doesn't count as talking, a follow-up missed more than 30 days ago no longer counts as planned, and a visit in the last 3 weeks, even a Not at Home, keeps someone out of Been a While. In data protection mode, Been a While stops at 90 days, when WitnessWork offers to delete old details. To take someone out of Been a While, long-press them and choose Not Now: they're dismissed for 30 days, and you can bring them back from Dismissed Contacts anytime. Each shows up to 5 contacts, and each contact appears only once. Everyone else follows under Other Contacts: favorites first, then current Bible studies, then past Bible studies, then by most recent visit. Your filters and Saved Views apply first, so the sections only include contacts the list would show. Empty sections are hidden, and if all four are empty the list is one plain list. Searching or choosing another sort also shows one plain list. Nearby is optional. It appears only if you've already allowed location for WitnessWork; the Contacts list never asks for it. It uses each contact's map pin, from their address or a pin you placed, so a contact without a location can't be Nearby. Your location is read on this device when you open Contacts, only to sort the list, and it isn't saved or sent anywhere. So rows don't move while you read, a new location shows the next time you open Contacts. To use another order, tap the Sort & Filter button (the sliders) at the top of Contacts and pick a sort; Reset returns to Suggested. If Nearby is missing, check that location is allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings and that the contact has a pin on the map. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names and addresses.

entries.question: How do follow-up, plan, and contact reminders work?

content.text: Turn on Notify Me when adding or editing a Follow-up or a Plan, then choose how long before it starts the reminder should arrive. A recurring Plan reminds you the same amount of time before each of its dates, counting from that date's own start time if you changed it for that date only. Dates you deleted, and dates after its end date, don't remind you. Each device schedules a recurring Plan's reminders up to two weeks ahead, so open WitnessWork at least every two weeks to keep them coming. Dismissing a contact also reminds you when they're available again. If Notify Me is off because notifications aren't allowed, turning it on asks for permission; if you've declined before, it opens your device settings. If a one-time Plan's or Follow-up's reminder time has already passed, the form says so and no reminder is sent. Rescheduling keeps the reminder time you chose. When a reminder arrives, it is also listed in the Home bell, even if system notifications are off, and tapping either one opens the follow-up, plan, or contact. Each device schedules its own reminders from your saved records, so after a sync or a backup restore, open WitnessWork once on that device to set them up. Deleting a visit, plan, or contact removes its reminders, including any already shown. With data protection mode on, reminders leave out names and topics. On Android, the system may deliver a reminder a few minutes late to save battery. If reminders don't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in Preferences and in your device settings, and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. On Android, reminders have their own Reminders category in WitnessWork's notification settings, separate from Buddies, so check that it's on. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.

entries.question: Why is there a number on the WitnessWork app icon?

content.text: On iOS, the number on the app icon is how many items in the Home notification bell you haven't read yet. News from your buddies, like a buddy's new badge or a reaction to yours, is never counted. Open the bell and scroll through it to mark items read; dismissing or clearing them also lowers the number. It updates while WitnessWork is open and when a Follow-up, Plan, or contact reminder arrives. Other items, like last month's report or a buddy's invitation, are counted the next time you open WitnessWork, so the number can be behind while the app is closed. Each device keeps its own count. The number needs notification permission; to hide it, turn off Badges for WitnessWork in your device's notification settings. That setting only affects this number, not the badges you grow on your profile. On Android, the app icon doesn't show an unread count; your launcher may show a dot for notifications in the notification shade. If the number looks wrong, open WitnessWork, then leave it to refresh the count. If it still doesn't match the bell, contact support from the Help Center.

entries.question: How do I turn off celebration and reminder sounds?

content.text: Open Settings → Preferences → Audio & Haptics and turn off Play sounds. This controls celebration chimes and reminders while WitnessWork is open; reminders still appear, just without sound (on Android, as a short message in the app). Reminders received while the app is closed follow your device's notification settings; adjust those separately if needed.

entries.question: How do I turn off vibrations?

content.text: Open Settings → Preferences → Audio & Haptics and turn off Haptics. WitnessWork then stops all of its vibration feedback, such as taps, chart scrubbing, and goal celebrations. The setting applies only to this device and isn't synced to your other devices. Some system controls, like menus and switches, may still vibrate based on your device's own settings; adjust those in your device's sound and haptics settings.

entries.question: How do I get directions to a contact?

content.text: Open the contact and tap their address. You'll be offered Apple Maps, Google Maps, or Waze depending on what's installed. You can also pin a contact's location without an address, which is useful for areas where street numbers don't exist.

entries.question: My pin is in the wrong place. Can I move it?

content.text: Yes. Open the contact's address screen and drag the pin to the correct spot. You can also place a pin without an address at all, which is helpful in areas without precise geolocation data.

entries.question: Why can't the map find my current location?

content.text: Check that location services are on and WitnessWork has location permission in your device's settings. Reopen the map and try again where your device can obtain a location. You can still enter an address or place a contact's pin manually without using your current location. If the problem continues, report the error with your device and operating-system version, leaving private contact details out of screenshots.

entries.question: Why are some contacts missing from the map?

content.text: The map shows your active contacts that have an address or a pin, and it uses the same filters as your Contacts list. Last-visit chips, Saved Views, and filters from Sort & Filter all apply to both, so a contact hidden from the list is hidden from the map too. The chips at the top of the map show what's on; tap All, tap the selected Saved View again, or open Sort & Filter (the sliders at the top) and tap Reset to see everyone. If the chips are tucked away after you move the map, tap the Contacts title to bring them back. The map's own search only narrows the pins further and doesn't change the list. A contact you create by dropping a pin stays on the map until you switch to the list, even if your filters would hide it. Dismissed contacts don't appear; find them under ••• → Dismissed Contacts. A contact without an address or pin can't appear either; open the contact and add an address or place its pin. A contact with an address but no pin yet, such as one from an import, appears once its address is looked up: when the map has any, tap Find contacts on the map at the top to look them all up, or tap X to hide it. This sends those addresses to the WitnessWork server, which looks them up with HERE, a mapping service, and doesn't keep them. An address that can't be found isn't offered again until you edit it; place that contact's pin by hand instead. In data protection mode, addresses are never looked up, so place pins by hand. A contact saved without an internet connection appears once you're back online with WitnessWork open; if it still doesn't, edit its address or place its pin. This works the same on iOS and Android, and filters are worked out on your device; they aren't shared. If a contact is still missing, check its address, then contact support from the Help Center and leave out names and addresses.

entries.question: What do the pins and cards on the map mean?

content.text: Each contact on the map is a round pin with their initials, colored by how long it's been since your last visit (tap the ⓘ button on the map to see what each color means, or change the colors in Settings → Preferences → Personalization → Color Key). A small mark on the pin's corner shows a follow-up that's overdue (red clock), a follow-up today (green clock), or a favorite (star).

Beside a pin, a card shows the contact's name and one detail. By default the detail is their next visit: an overdue follow-up, an upcoming follow-up with its day and time, or otherwise when you last visited. Cards for overdue and upcoming follow-ups are placed first, and cards that would cover another pin or card wait until you zoom in, so zoom in to see more. The selected contact's card turns green.

To choose what cards show, go to Settings → Preferences → Map, or tap the layers button on the map and choose Pin cards show. You can pick Next visit, Last visit, Follow-up topic, Name only, or any of your contact fields, such as a Language field when you work a language territory. A card shows only the name when that contact has no topic or no value in the field.

When pins sit on top of each other, they gather into one square pin with a count. Tap it: contacts at the same address, such as an apartment building, open in a list with their apartment or unit, most urgent first, and tapping a name selects that contact. Contacts that are only close together zoom the map in so their pins spread out.

The chip at the top of the map counts the contacts in view who are overdue or due in the next seven days. Tap it to keep only them bright, with their cards, and tap it again to see everyone. When today has a route, the Today's Route chip opens it. To plan a route from contacts on the map, see "How do I plan a route from the map?".

Pins and cards are worked out on your device and nothing is sent anywhere to draw them. The map doesn't rotate or tilt, so the cards stay next to their pins. This works the same on iPhone, iPad, and Android, and it's free. If a contact is missing from the map, see "Why are some contacts missing from the map?". If a card shows the wrong detail, check the contact's follow-up or field value; for other problems, use the Help Center's private support option and keep names and addresses out of public reports.

entries.question: How do I plan a route from the map?

content.text: On the Contacts map, tap the Select contacts button (the dotted lasso in the column of buttons on the left). Then tap pins to pick contacts, or draw a loop around pins with one finger to pick everyone inside it. Tap a square pin with a count to pick every contact in it. Tap Select Due to add everyone in view who is overdue or due in the next seven days. While you select, one finger draws instead of moving the map; pinch to zoom, or tap Done to move the map again.

Tap Plan Route to open today's route with the contacts you picked added after its stops, most urgent first. Contacts already on today's route, such as one with a follow-up today, aren't added twice. A route holds up to 10 stops, so Plan Route waits until your picks fit in the room today's route has left, which the bar shows when you pick too many; tap Clear to start over. From there, use Shortest Order, set how long you'll stay at each stop, and tap Start Route, as described in "How do I plan a route for my service day?".

Route planning is a Supporter feature. Anyone can select contacts and open the route to see the stops on the map; Shortest Order and Start Route need Supporter. When today already has a route, the Today's Route chip at the top of the map opens it.

Selecting contacts never changes them, their follow-ups, or your plans. The route is saved on this device for today and isn't synced to your other devices. This works the same on iPhone, iPad, and Android. If Plan Route stays dimmed, pick at least one contact and no more than the route has room for. If a contact you picked isn't on the route, the route was full: the route builder says how many didn't fit. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support option and keep names and addresses out of public reports.

entries.question: Can I add a photo to a contact?

content.text: Yes. Open a contact, tap the avatar, and pick a photo from your library or take a new one. This is especially handy when contacts share names or when a photo helps you spot the right door.

entries.question: How do I hide a contact without deleting them?

content.text: Open the contact and tap "Dismiss." You'll pick how long to dismiss them for (1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, or 1 year). The contact disappears from your active lists for that period and then comes back automatically when the time is up. If notifications are enabled, you'll also get a reminder when they reappear, so dismissed contacts won't quietly slip through the cracks. You can find or restore dismissed contacts at any time from the link at the bottom of your Contacts list, the ••• menu in Contacts, or Settings → Dismissed Contacts.

entries.question: What's the difference between archiving and deleting a contact?

content.text: Touch and hold a contact in Contacts or on the map, or open it and tap More (•••), then choose Archive or Delete Permanently…. In Select mode, use Archive or Delete at the bottom. Swiping a contact from the right archives it. Archiving hides the contact and keeps it and every conversation logged with them. Restore it within 90 days from Settings → More → Recover Contacts; after that its details are removed. Deleting permanently erases the contact, every conversation logged with them, and their photos, on this device and on devices that sync with it through Cloud Sync, iCloud Sync, or Google Drive Sync. It can't be undone, so WitnessWork asks first and offers Archive Instead. To delete a contact you already archived, touch and hold it in Recover Contacts and choose Delete Permanently…. With data protection mode on there's no Archive: removing a contact always deletes it. To hide a contact only for a while, use Dismiss For instead. Backup files you saved earlier still contain deleted contacts. If you deleted one by mistake, it can only come back by restoring a backup made before the delete, which replaces your current data, so create a fresh backup first. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.

entries.question: How do I see which contacts are due for a visit?

content.text: Below the search field in Contacts, tap a chip to show only contacts in that group: Stale, This month, This week, or Never contacted. Each chip shows how many active contacts it holds, and its color matches the contact's pin on the map. Swipe the chips sideways to see them all. Tap the chip again, or tap All, to show everyone. The same chips sit at the top of the map, where they count only contacts with a location and filter the pins; they tuck away while you move the map, so tap the Contacts title to bring them back. To change their order, touch a chip, pause briefly, then drag it along the row; All stays first. The order is a preference, so it's included in backups and syncs with your other devices when sync is on. Groups are based on your most recent visit, and "Not at homes" count as visits. To change when a contact moves between groups, or the colors, tap the info button at the end of the chips (on the map, the legend button) and then the pencil. A chip adds a filter you can also see and remove in Sort & Filter, and it applies to the list and the map alike. Dismissed contacts aren't counted. Nothing is shared; the groups are worked out on your device.

entries.question: How do I find contacts with no follow-up planned?

content.text: In Contacts, tap the Sort & Filter button (the sliders) at the top, tap Add filter, choose Follow-up, then pick a value and tap Apply. Upcoming shows contacts with a follow-up that's still ahead and that you haven't visited since. None upcoming shows everyone else, so you can find people you haven't planned a return visit for. Missed shows contacts whose follow-up passed more than 4 hours ago, within the last 30 days, with no visit since: the same people as your missed follow-up reminders. Dismissed follow-ups don't count. To see who's next, choose Next follow-up under Sort: each contact then shows when their follow-up is due in place of their last visit. The soonest follow-up comes first with Descending, the latest with Ascending, then missed follow-ups, and contacts with none go last. Other sorts, like Bible Study, Date added, or City, show the value they sort by in the same place. Follow-up filters work on iOS and Android, apply to the list and the map alike, and can be part of a saved view. They're worked out on your device, and nothing is shared. If a contact appears where you don't expect, open their most recent visit and check its follow-up date, or whether a later visit already answered it. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.

entries.question: Where are Map, Buddies, and Settings?

content.text: The bottom bar shows Home, Schedule, Contacts, and Progress, with Add beside them for logging time, creating a Plan, or adding a contact. Progress and Add Time appear when your role logs hours. Map is inside Contacts: tap the map button beside the Contacts title, and WitnessWork opens the view you used last. Buddies, when available on iOS, opens from the Buddies button at the top of Schedule. View Report at the top of Progress opens the Service Report for the month you're viewing. Tap your profile picture at the top left of any main screen for Profile (your role, time served, and stats), Settings, Support, and Help Center; on a wide tablet layout, Settings also stays in the sidebar. If you hid the sidebar, tap Show sidebar in the page header to bring it back. If you turned on Hide Donate Heart, Support is left out of that menu and stays in Settings. Your contacts, plans, and records are unchanged; only where you find them moved. If something still seems missing, update the app, then use Still need help? below.

entries.question: How do I report a bug or request a feature?

content.text: Use the buttons below to report a bug or request a feature. Include the steps to reproduce it, what you expected, your device and operating-system version, and the WitnessWork version shown under Still need help?. Remove private contact details, notes, account IDs, and Buddies Codes or invite links from public reports and screenshots. For backup or other sensitive problems, use the private email link in Still need help? instead. Source code, the Privacy Policy, and Terms of Use are under Settings → About.

entries.question: Which languages does WitnessWork support, and how do I change or report a translation?

content.text: WitnessWork is available in 19 languages: Arabic, Bemba, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Kinyarwanda, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Ukrainian, and Vietnamese. It follows your device's language by default (Device Default). To pick another, open Settings and change Language at the top; WitnessWork restarts in that language. You can also set a language for WitnessWork alone in your phone's settings: on iPhone and iPad, Settings → Apps → WitnessWork → Language (shown once your device has more than one preferred language); on Android 13 or later, Settings → Apps → WitnessWork → Language. With Device Default, WitnessWork follows that choice, and a language picked inside WitnessWork takes priority. If your language isn't supported, the app shows English. Some text is drawn by your phone, so it follows your phone's language instead: alert buttons, date pickers, share sheets, and the widget gallery. On iPhone and iPad, the explanations in permission requests (location, camera, microphone, and others) are still in English. Translations are made with AI, so a word or phrase may sometimes be off, especially terms Jehovah's Witnesses use in a particular way. To report one, use the email link in Still need help? and include your language, the screen, the text you see, and what it should say. A screenshot helps; cover names, addresses, and notes first. Corrections arrive in a later app update. There is no longer a volunteer translation project to join.

entries.question: How does WitnessWork work in Arabic and right to left?

content.text: Choose العربية under Settings → Language, or set your phone to Arabic and keep Device Default. WitnessWork restarts and reads right to left: screens, menus, swipe actions, progress bars, and charts are mirrored, and back arrows point the other way. Numbers show in Arabic-Indic digits (٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩), and months use the names in Jehovah's Witnesses' Arabic publications, such as تشرين الأول (أكتوبر). When you enter hours, goals, or mileage, you can type Arabic-Indic or Latin digits. Names, phone numbers, addresses, and notes stay exactly as you typed them. Phone numbers and email addresses read left to right, and numbers you type into a field stay in the order you typed them. Date order, the clock, and the first day of the week follow your Format Region in Settings → Preferences → Region & Formats: choose Middle East (Arabic) there for weeks that start on Saturday, or leave it on Auto (Device) to follow your phone. Widgets and the Apple Watch and Wear OS apps follow WitnessWork's language and direction after the app has opened once. Searching contacts and help finds Arabic words with or without vowel marks. Your records are stored the same way in every language, so switching to another language, or back, changes only how they are shown.

entries.question: Where are the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, and open-source licenses?

content.text: Tap your profile picture, then Settings, and scroll to About. It links to the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, and WitnessWork's source code. Where Scribe AI is available, it also links to the OpenRouter ZDR policy that covers what you send to Scribe AI. Open Source Licenses lists every open-source package WitnessWork is built with, along with its version, license, and author; tap a package to open its page, which shows the full license and source. Search by package name, license, or author. Long-press any link to copy or share it.

entries.question: What does Debugging Tools do?

content.text: Debugging Tools helps troubleshoot problems with support. Turn it on in Settings → Advanced; it applies only to the device you turn it on for, on iOS and Android. It adds a Tools tab with diagnostic, test-data, and repair actions, shows extra technical details on some screens, and turns on more detailed diagnostic logging. Some Tools actions add sample data or permanently delete data, so only use them when support asks, and back up first under Settings → Backup & Restore. Turning the switch on or off doesn't change your data; turn it off to hide the Tools tab and details again.

entries.question: What do I get as a supporter?

content.text: An active Supporter subscription gives you the Supporter badge, custom accent colors and Plan Today's Route, which puts the day's follow-ups and plans in the shortest driving order, plus Device Sync, and alternate app icons on iOS. Device Sync is Cloud Sync, the only option that syncs live, even between iPhone and Android, or iCloud Sync on iOS and Google Drive Sync on Android. Supporters also get generous Scribe AI limits on iOS and Android; without Supporter, Scribe AI has a smaller monthly limit (see How do Scribe AI limits work?). Core features remain free, including contact filters, sorting and saved views, and Buddies when available; Supporters can also choose each buddy's color. A one-time Tip gives Donor recognition but does not activate Supporter features.

entries.question: I already paid, but Supporter features or prices are missing. What should I do?

content.text: Check your connection and that your device's store uses the account you purchased with. If you opened WitnessWork without a connection, prices and your Supporter status load by themselves once you're back online. Open Settings → Become a supporter and use Restore Purchases when it is shown. A one-time Tip does not activate Supporter features. If no purchases are found, prices do not load, or your subscription still is not recognized, email support privately with your app version and what happened. If support needs your account ID, use the support button in this screen's header to open Still need help?, then tap Copy Account ID. Share that ID privately. Restoring purchases restores access, not your service records.

entries.question: What is a Founding Supporter?

content.text: Founding Supporters were already supporting WitnessWork before the Supporter tier launched in May 2026, when support came with no perks at all. The label is simply our thank-you. It isn't a separate tier: Founding Supporters get the same features as every other Supporter, and it can't be purchased or earned now. While your support is active, Founding Supporter appears on your profile and in Settings. It comes from your Supporter start date, so nothing extra is stored or shared. If your support lapses, the label is hidden until you support again. It returns if your store account still reports your original start date, which is usually the case when you resubscribe with the same account. If you expected to see it, open Settings → Become a supporter and use Restore Purchases. If it still doesn't appear, use the support button in this screen's header to open Still need help? and contact support privately.

entries.question: Is WitnessWork still free?

content.text: Yes — and always will be. Every core feature stays free for everyone. Supporting is completely optional; it helps fund ongoing development and unlocks a few personal touches as a thank-you.

entries.question: What happens if I stop supporting?

content.text: To stop, open Settings → Manage subscription and choose Cancel or change subscription, or cancel in your App Store or Google Play subscriptions. Supporter access continues until the end of the period you've paid for, and your existing data and local backups remain available. After that, sync pauses while Supporter access is unavailable. If sync was on, it resumes when access returns; an explicit choice to turn it off stays off. Photo sync follows its own setting. Your accent color and app icon return to the defaults, but your choices are kept for when you support again. Check Settings → Device Sync for the current status. If you only need a break, you can pause instead.

entries.question: Can I pause my support instead of cancelling?

content.text: Yes. Open Settings → Manage subscription. On iPhone and iPad, choose to pause payments for 1, 3, or 6 months. The pause starts when your current period ends. You aren't charged during it, and Supporter features stay on, including sync, your accent color, and app icon. Payments then resume automatically at the same amount on the date shown, and you can still cancel anytime in your App Store subscriptions. You can pause once every 12 months; the pause dates are saved with your settings so your other devices respect them. On Android, choose Pause in Google Play to pause a monthly subscription for 1 to 3 months. Supporter features such as the badge and accent color pause too, then return automatically with your settings kept, and you can resume early in Google Play. Pause options don't appear during a free trial, a payment problem, a Family Sharing subscription, or within 12 months of your last pause. If a pause fails, nothing changes; try again later or manage your subscription in your store. For anything else, use Still need help? to contact support privately.

entries.question: Why are you accepting donations?

content.text: As a brother in the hall, I consider it a privilege to be able to use my skills to help others in the congregation. Although free to everyone, developing, running, and maintaining this application, unfortunately costs a significant amount of money and time. I view donating as similar to how one might pay for another's gas after going in service with them - it's a loving gesture that goes greatly appreciated.

entries.question: What are the donations used for?

content.text: Your donation helps keeps this app running! There are costs with purchasing real devices as development equipment, paying for location API service fees, build service API fees, app store fees, and opportunity cost of my many hours spent developing this app. Each piece of support is greatly appreciated!

entries.question: Where can I see what changed in the latest update?

content.text: Tap your profile picture, then Settings → What's New, for a summary of recent changes. Big updates also open a short tour the first time you launch after updating. If you choose Later, the notification bell keeps a shortcut to it, and What's New has a button to take the tour again.

entries.question: How do I get the latest WitnessWork update?

content.text: Most updates download by themselves while you use WitnessWork. When one is ready, the bell on Home shows Update Ready. Tap Update Now, and WitnessWork restarts into the new version right away. If you'd rather wait, dismiss it or leave it there: the update applies the next time WitnessWork starts after you close it completely. Restarting doesn't touch your service records, contacts, or notes; everything you've saved is there afterward.

To look for an update yourself, tap your profile picture, then Settings → More → Check for update. Some updates need a new version from the App Store, or the Google Play Store app on Android, so keep automatic updates on there too. If an update won't download, connect to the internet and try Check for update again.

entries.question: What's in the bell on Home?

content.text: The bell at the top of Home collects reminders and updates, so they wait there instead of piling up on Home when you open the app. You'll find things like last month's Service Report, a pending time rollover, backup and data protection reminders, missed Follow-ups, reminders that already went off, new badges and new items for your pet that you haven't looked at yet, Buddies activity (where Buddies is available), and What's New. The red badge counts items you haven't seen yet. News from your buddies, like a buddy's new badge or a reaction to yours, sits at the bottom under From your buddies and never adds to that number; a small dot on the bell means some of it is new. Tap an item to act on it, tap X to dismiss it, or tap Clear All. Invitations and requests still waiting for your answer stay until you respond. A dismissed item doesn't come back. Which items you've seen or dismissed is remembered on this device only.

entries.question: How do I share WitnessWork with a friend?

content.text: Tap your profile picture, then Settings → Share WitnessWork. Pick Android or iPhone, and your friend can scan the code with their phone's camera to open WitnessWork in Google Play or the App Store. Share Link sends a message with both store links, so it works for anyone. WitnessWork is free on both. The message only contains the store links — nothing about you or your records. If a code won't scan, turn up your screen's brightness or use Share Link instead.

entries.question: Is WitnessWork on Android?

content.text: Yes. WitnessWork is back on Google Play, and it's free. Time and reports, the timer, contacts and follow-ups, plans, the map (with Google Maps), mileage, reminders, and backups all work on Android. Buddies works on Android too, including with buddies on iPhone. Supporters can keep their devices in sync with Cloud Sync, which also syncs with an iPhone, or with Google Drive Sync between Android devices. A few features rely on Apple services and stay on iPhone and iPad: iCloud Sync, widgets, Live Activities, and app icons. Scribe AI works on Android too. To move to a new phone on either platform, use Set Up Another Device on the old phone (Settings → Account); with Cloud Sync, the new phone gets your records without a restore step, or it offers to restore your Backup if you turned it on in Settings → Account. You can also create a backup file (Settings → Backup & Restore → Create Backup), copy it to the new phone, then choose From a backup file on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen. Between Android devices you can also choose From Google Drive there. Keep backup files private; they can contain householder details.

entries.question: Is my data private and secure?

content.text: Yes. WitnessWork has no sign-up and no ads, and your records live on your device. Anything that leaves it is encrypted or anonymized, so it isn't tied to you. Your account is anonymous: no email, phone number, or password. If you turn on Backup (Settings → Account), WitnessWork's server keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy of your records that only your devices can read, not WitnessWork; it's off unless you turn it on. Cloud Sync keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy of each device's data on WitnessWork's server that only your devices can read. iCloud Sync and Google Drive Sync go straight to your own account over an encrypted connection, never through WitnessWork's servers; on iPhone and iPad, turning on Apple's Advanced Data Protection makes iCloud end-to-end encrypted. Buddies is end-to-end encrypted, so only you and your buddies can read what you share. A shared contact travels inside its link and isn't stored by WitnessWork. Scribe AI sends what you ask it over an encrypted connection to Zero Data Retention providers that don't store it, and route planning sends only map coordinates. Usage statistics are anonymous counts that never include names, contacts, reports, or notes; turn them off anytime in Settings → Preferences → Share Anonymous Usage Statistics. Supporter purchases use a random identifier, not your name or email. Backup files you export are yours, so keep them somewhere private; they can include householder details. WitnessWork deletes its own temporary copies of exported backups, shared contact files, and picked photos the next time it starts and when you permanently delete householder data. For privacy questions, use the private support link in the Help Center.
